chunks.title: Anchor bolt specification for floor-mounted R-series robots
chunks.text: The robot base must be secured to the foundation using four M16 hexagon socket head cap bolts of property class 12.9. Tighten each anchor bolt to 210 N-m in a diagonal sequence, applying the load in two stages of approximately half torque followed by full torque. The concrete foundation shall be at least 300 mm thick with a compressive strength of 18 MPa or greater. Where a fabricated steel stand is used in place of direct floor mounting, the stand must transmit the full reaction moment without permanent deformation. Re-check anchor bolt torque after the first 100 hours of operation and at every periodic inspection thereafter. Loose anchor bolts permit the base to rock under high acceleration, which degrades repeatability and accelerates reducer wear.

chunks.title: Mounting surface flatness and levelness tolerance
chunks.text: The mounting surface beneath the robot base must be flat to within 0.5 mm measured across the full bolt circle diameter. Levelness should be held within 0.5 degrees of horizontal for standard floor installation. Shim packs may be used to correct local high spots, but each shim must span the full width of the base flange rather than sitting under a single bolt boss. Do not attempt to pull an uneven base flat by overtightening the anchor bolts, as this preloads the casting and can crack the base. After shimming, verify with a precision level in two perpendicular axes and grout the gap if the shim stack exceeds 3 mm. An out-of-tolerance mounting surface introduces a fixed positional offset that mastering cannot fully compensate.

chunks.title: Declaring non-standard mounting orientation in controller configuration
chunks.text: Robots installed in ceiling-suspended or wall-hung attitudes require the mounting orientation parameter to be declared in the controller before the first motion command. The servo system uses this declaration to compute the gravity torque feedforward term for each joint. If the orientation is left at the factory default of floor mounting while the arm is physically inverted, the gravity compensation is applied with the wrong sign. The resulting symptoms are joint droop when servos are released, overshoot on downward moves, and intermittent overload alarms on the shoulder axis. Wall-mounted installations additionally impose reduced swing limits on the first joint, which must be entered as software travel limits. Always re-run mastering verification after changing the declared orientation.

chunks.title: Removal of shipping brackets and transport fixtures
chunks.text: Newly delivered manipulators are secured with painted yellow transport brackets bolted between the upper arm and the base casting. All transport brackets, shipping bolts, and axis restraint straps must be removed before the controller is powered on for the first time. Attempting to jog the arm with a bracket still fitted will produce an immediate overload or deviation alarm and may bend the bracket into the casting. Retain the brackets and their fasteners in the crate, as they are required whenever the robot is relocated. Record the removal on the installation checklist and confirm each axis moves freely by hand where the brake release permits. Do not discard the desiccant bags or the packing list until commissioning is complete.

chunks.title: Stiffness requirement for customer-fabricated support structures
chunks.text: A customer-built pedestal or gantry supporting the manipulator must have a first natural frequency at least 1.5 times higher than the highest motion frequency generated by the robot. For most six-axis models this means the support structure should be stiffer than 30 Hz in both bending and torsion. Insufficient structural stiffness allows the base to deflect in reaction to arm acceleration, producing a low-frequency sway that the servo loop cannot observe or correct. Because the encoders measure joint angle rather than absolute tool position, this deflection appears as a position error that no amount of gain tuning will remove. Reinforce open-section columns with gussets and ensure the baseplate is welded continuously rather than stitch welded. Verify by measuring tool-point deflection with a dial indicator while the arm executes a worst-case acceleration profile.

chunks.text_ko: 매니퓰레이터를 지지하는 사용자 제작 받침대나 갠트리는 로봇이 발생시키는 최고 동작 주파수보다 최소 1.5배 높은 1차 고유 진동수를 가져야 합니다. 대부분의 6축 모델에서는 굽힘과 비틀림 양방향으로 30 Hz 이상의 강성이 요구됩니다. 구조 강성이 부족하면 암 가속의 반력으로 베이스가 변형되어 서보 루프가 관측하거나 보정할 수 없는 저주파 흔들림이 발생합니다. 엔코더는 절대적인 공구 위치가 아니라 관절 각도를 측정하므로 이러한 변형은 게인 튜닝으로 제거할 수 없는 위치 오차로 나타납니다. 개방 단면 기둥은 거싯으로 보강하고 베이스 플레이트는 단속 용접이 아니라 연속 용접으로 시공하십시오. 최악 조건의 가속 프로파일을 실행하면서 다이얼 게이지로 공구 선단 변형량을 측정하여 검증하십시오.

chunks.title: Primary supply voltage and breaker sizing for the E controller
chunks.text: The E series controller accepts a three-phase supply of 200 to 220 V AC at 50 or 60 Hz, with an allowable deviation of plus or minus 10 percent. Voltage outside this window causes the DC bus to trip on undervoltage during high acceleration even when the idle reading appears normal. Size the upstream circuit breaker at 30 A for standard payload models, and use a type D or motor-rated characteristic to tolerate the inrush of the charging circuit. A dedicated feeder is strongly recommended; sharing a circuit with welding equipment introduces voltage sag that the controller interprets as a supply fault. The earth leakage breaker must be rated for at least 200 mA sensitivity because the drive output filters produce continuous leakage current. Confirm phase rotation before first power-on.

chunks.title: Separation of motor power and encoder signal cabling
chunks.text: Motor power cables and encoder signal cables must be routed in separate trays or conduits with a minimum spacing of 200 mm along any parallel run. Where the two must cross, they shall cross at right angles rather than running alongside each other. The pulse-width modulated output of the drive stage produces steep voltage transients that couple capacitively into adjacent low-level signal pairs. Symptoms of poor separation include intermittent encoder communication faults that appear only when the arm is moving at high speed. Do not bundle field device wiring, valve solenoid returns, or welding cable into the same tray as the robot signal harness. Terminate the encoder cable shield at the controller end only to avoid a ground loop.

chunks.title: Protective earth bonding and ground electrode resistance
chunks.text: The controller enclosure and the manipulator base must each be bonded to the plant protective earth using a conductor of at least 5.5 square millimetres cross section. Measured resistance from the bonding point to the ground electrode shall not exceed 100 ohms for class D installations. Use a dedicated bonding stud with a serrated washer and remove paint from the contact area to achieve metal-to-metal contact. Daisy-chaining the earth connection from one machine to the next is prohibited because a single loosened lug then disconnects several machines at once. Poor bonding manifests as erratic digital input readings, unexplained communication dropouts, and a tingling sensation when touching the enclosure. Verify continuity with a low-resistance ohmmeter rather than a standard multimeter.

chunks.title: X1 and X2 connector pin assignment on the controller interface panel
chunks.text: Connector X1 on the controller interface panel carries the external emergency stop and safety interlock circuits on pins 1 through 8. Pins 1 and 2 form the first emergency stop channel, pins 3 and 4 the second channel, and pins 5 through 8 the safety fence interlock pair. Connector X2 carries general purpose digital I/O, with pins 1 through 16 assigned to inputs and pins 17 through 32 assigned to outputs. Both connectors use a screw-locking D-subminiature shell that must be fully seated and secured before the safety circuit will validate. Unused safety pins must be jumpered only during bench testing and never in a production installation. Refer to the wiring diagram supplied with the controller for the exact revision of the interface panel fitted to your unit.
chunks.query: X1 and X2 connector pin assignment on the controller interface panel

chunks.title: Bend radius and torsion limits for the dress pack
chunks.text: The dress pack carrying air lines and tool cabling must maintain a bend radius of at least ten times the outer diameter of the largest hose in the bundle. Torsional twist across any single segment must not exceed 90 degrees during the full motion cycle. Anchor the bundle at the base and at the upper arm so that motion is distributed across the free length rather than concentrated at a clamp. Repeated flexing beyond the rated radius work-hardens the copper conductors and produces intermittent open circuits that are extremely difficult to diagnose. Inspect the bundle for helical kinking, jacket abrasion, and clamp migration at every periodic inspection. Replace the entire loom rather than splicing an individual damaged conductor.

chunks.title: Dual-channel emergency stop wiring and cross monitoring
chunks.text: The emergency stop circuit is implemented as two independent normally closed channels that are cross monitored by the safety relay in the controller. Both channels must open within 200 milliseconds of each other or the controller latches a channel discrepancy fault requiring a manual reset. Wire each channel through a separate conductor pair and avoid routing both channels through a single multi-core cable where a crush injury could short them together. Series connection of multiple emergency stop devices is permitted provided the total loop resistance stays below 20 ohms. A single-channel connection or a jumper across one channel defeats the fault detection and reduces the achieved performance level. Test both channels independently during commissioning by opening one at a time and confirming the discrepancy fault appears.
chunks.query: dual-channel emergency stop wiring with cross monitoring and channel discrepancy fault

chunks.title: Reduced speed limit of 250 mm/s in teach mode
chunks.text: When the mode selector is set to teach, the controller limits the tool centre point velocity to 250 mm per second regardless of the programmed speed. This limit is enforced by the safety processor independently of the motion planner and cannot be overridden from the program. Check mode permits program verification at reduced speed with the enabling device held in the centre position. If the monitored velocity exceeds the limit, the safety processor issues a category 0 stop and reports a speed monitoring violation. The limit applies to the tool centre point, so a long end effector can exceed the flange speed limit while the wrist appears to move slowly. Verify the configured tool length is accurate, otherwise the monitored speed will not reflect the true hazard.
chunks.query: 250 mm/s reduced speed limit in teach mode
chunks.text_ko: 모드 선택 스위치가 티치 모드에 있을 때 컨트롤러는 프로그래밍된 속도와 관계없이 툴 센터 포인트 속도를 250 mm/s로 제한합니다. 이 제한은 모션 플래너와 독립적으로 안전 프로세서에 의해 강제되며 프로그램에서 무효화할 수 없습니다. 체크 모드에서는 인에이블 장치를 중간 위치에 유지한 상태로 감속 속도에서 프로그램 검증이 가능합니다. 감시된 속도가 제한을 초과하면 안전 프로세서는 카테고리 0 정지를 실행하고 속도 감시 위반을 보고합니다. 이 제한은 툴 센터 포인트에 적용되므로 긴 엔드 이펙터를 장착한 경우 손목이 느리게 보여도 실제 속도는 한계를 초과할 수 있습니다. 설정된 공구 길이가 정확한지 확인하십시오. 그렇지 않으면 감시 속도가 실제 위험을 반영하지 못합니다.

chunks.title: Three-position enabling device behaviour on the teach pendant
chunks.text: The teach pendant enabling switch has three distinct positions: fully released, centre, and fully squeezed. Servo power is permitted only while the switch is held in the centre detent, and is removed in both the released and the fully squeezed states. This arrangement ensures that a startled operator who either lets go or clenches the grip will bring the arm to a stop. The switch must be released completely and then returned to centre before servo power can be re-enabled, preventing a squeeze-through recovery. Two independent contact sets are monitored for agreement, and a discrepancy lasting longer than one second reports a fault. Never defeat the enabling device with a cable tie or wedge, as this removes the primary protective measure during manual intervention.

chunks.title: Perimeter guard gate interlock and restart requirements
chunks.text: Each access gate in the perimeter guarding must be fitted with an interlock device that removes servo power when the gate is opened. The interlock must use a coded actuator or a guard-locking device where the hazard does not cease immediately upon power removal. Opening a gate during automatic operation initiates a protective stop and latches the condition until an acknowledgement is given from outside the guarded space. The acknowledgement station must be positioned so that the operator can see the entire enclosed area, preventing a restart while a colleague remains inside. Where the enclosure is large enough for a person to be concealed, an additional presence-sensing device or a trapped-key sequence is required. Simple sequential restart from inside the cell is not acceptable.

chunks.title: Cubic-S dual check safety zone configuration
chunks.text: The Cubic-S safety unit provides dual check monitoring of position and speed using two independent processors that compare results every control cycle. Protected zones are defined as rectangular prisms or as planes in the robot base coordinate system, and each zone may be configured as either a keep-in or keep-out region. Zone violation triggers a category 0 or category 1 stop according to the configured reaction. The unit also provides safe tool orientation monitoring and safe standstill detection for collaborative arrangements. Configuration is performed with the dedicated setup tool and must be protected by a password, with the resulting parameter set recorded in the cell validation file. Any change to the zone definition requires the entire safety function to be revalidated and the checksum recorded.
chunks.query: Cubic-S dual check safety zone configuration for keep-out regions

chunks.title: Alarm E1023 servo overload on a single axis
chunks.text: Alarm E1023 indicates that the thermal model of a servo motor has exceeded its permissible accumulated load. The controller computes an integrated current-squared-time value and trips when the calculated winding temperature passes the limit. Common causes are payload above the rated value, an incorrectly registered tool inertia, a mechanical binding in the joint, or a failed brake that has not released. Allow the motor to cool for at least twenty minutes before resetting, as an immediate reset restarts the integration from a high initial value. Check the actual current draw in the servo monitor screen against the rated continuous current for that axis. Persistent E1023 on the same axis after payload verification indicates a mechanical fault rather than a programming problem.
chunks.query: alarm E1023 servo overload on one axis

chunks.title: Alarm D1102 encoder communication error
chunks.text: Alarm D1102 is raised when the serial encoder response frame is corrupted or missing for more than the permitted number of consecutive control cycles. The most frequent root cause is electrical noise coupling into the encoder cable rather than a genuine encoder failure. Inspect the cable for damage at the flex points, confirm the shield is terminated at the controller end, and verify separation from motor power runs. A loose connector at the motor end will produce the fault intermittently and typically only during high-speed motion. If the alarm occurs immediately at power-on with the arm stationary, suspect the encoder itself or the interface board. Record the axis number reported alongside the alarm code, as the diagnosis differs for the wrist axes which share a common cable route.

chunks.title: Manual brake release procedure and brake fault diagnosis
chunks.text: Each axis is fitted with a spring-applied electromagnetic brake that engages whenever servo power is removed. Manual release is performed with the dedicated brake release unit connected to the release connector inside the base cover, and requires 24 V DC to be applied to the selected axis coil. Before releasing any brake, support the arm mechanically because the limb will fall under gravity as soon as the brake opens. A brake that fails to release produces an overload alarm shortly after motion begins, while a brake that fails to engage allows the arm to drift downward after servo power is removed. Measure the coil resistance and compare against the value in the maintenance table to distinguish a failed coil from a failed driver circuit. Never operate the robot with a defective brake on a gravity-loaded axis.

chunks.title: Controller cabinet over-temperature and filter blockage
chunks.text: The controller monitors internal ambient temperature and issues a warning at 50 degrees Celsius followed by a shutdown at 60 degrees Celsius. The most common cause of a rising trend is a clogged intake filter mat restricting airflow through the cabinet. Filters should be inspected monthly in clean environments and weekly where grinding dust, weld smoke, or textile lint is present. Verify that the cabinet doors seal properly, since an open door disrupts the designed airflow path and can raise internal temperature despite the apparent ventilation. Confirm the cooling fans spin freely and that the exhaust is not obstructed by adjacent equipment or stacked material. Sustained operation near the warning threshold shortens the life of the electrolytic capacitors in the drive stage.

chunks.title: Diagnosing a broken chain in the enabling circuit
chunks.text: When servo power cannot be established in manual mode and no explicit alarm is displayed, the fault usually lies somewhere in the series enabling chain. This chain runs from the pendant grip switch through the mode selector contacts, the pendant connection interlock, and the safety relay input terminals. Use the safety signal monitor screen to observe the state of each element in the chain rather than measuring voltages at random terminals. A pendant that has been unplugged without the bypass plug fitted will hold the chain open with no alarm text. Corroded contacts in the mode selector are a frequent cause on machines that have been in service for several years. Work through the chain from the source terminal outward and record the first element that shows an unexpected state.

chunks.title: Grease type and replacement interval for the JT1 to JT3 reducers
chunks.text: The reduction gears on joints JT1 through JT3 are packed with a lithium-soap grease of consistency NLGI 0 conforming to the specification listed in the maintenance section. The nominal replacement interval is 12000 operating hours or four years, whichever occurs first, reduced to 6000 hours for duty cycles above 70 percent. Purge the old grease through the drain port until fresh grease emerges, then run the axis through its full travel to distribute the charge before refitting the drain plug. Overfilling raises the internal pressure and forces grease past the oil seals into the motor cavity. Never mix grease types, as the soap bases are incompatible and the mixture will separate and harden. Record the date and the quantity injected in the maintenance log.

chunks.text_ko: JT1부터 JT3까지의 감속 기어에는 유지보수 항목에 명시된 규격에 적합한 NLGI 0 등급의 리튬 비누기 그리스가 충전되어 있습니다. 표준 교환 주기는 12000 운전 시간 또는 4년 중 먼저 도래하는 시점이며, 가동률 70퍼센트를 초과하는 경우 6000시간으로 단축됩니다. 배출 포트를 통해 새 그리스가 나올 때까지 기존 그리스를 밀어내고, 배출 플러그를 다시 장착하기 전에 축을 전체 가동 범위로 구동하여 충전량을 고르게 분포시키십시오. 과충전하면 내부 압력이 상승하여 그리스가 오일 실을 통과해 모터 공간으로 유입됩니다. 비누기가 서로 호환되지 않아 분리되고 경화되므로 서로 다른 종류의 그리스를 절대 혼합하지 마십시오. 주입 날짜와 수량을 유지보수 일지에 기록하십시오.

chunks.title: Encoder backup battery replacement
chunks.text: Absolute position data is retained by lithium backup batteries housed in the base cover while the controller is powered off. The batteries have a nominal service life of two years and should be replaced on a scheduled basis rather than waiting for the low voltage warning. Replace the batteries with the controller powered on so that the encoder retains its count from the main supply during the exchange. If the batteries are removed with the controller off, the absolute position is lost on every affected axis and mastering must be performed again. Use only the specified lithium cell type, as alkaline substitutes have a different discharge curve and will trigger nuisance warnings. Dispose of the old cells according to local regulations and record the replacement date on the cover label.

chunks.title: Measuring accumulated lost motion in the reduction gears
chunks.text: Wear in a harmonic reduction gear appears first as an increase in lost motion, measured by applying a known torque in each direction at the output and recording the angular difference. Mount a dial indicator against the arm at a known radius, lock the motor shaft, and apply the test torque specified for the axis in the maintenance table. A reading beyond three arc-minutes for the wrist axes or two arc-minutes for the main axes indicates the flexspline is approaching the end of its fatigue life. Rising lost motion presents in production as path deviation on direction reversals and as a repeatability figure that has drifted from the commissioning baseline. Trend the measurement across successive inspections rather than judging a single reading, since the absolute value varies with temperature. Replace the gear unit as an assembly; individual components are not separately serviceable.

chunks.title: Timing belt tension for the JT4 and JT5 wrist axes
chunks.text: The JT4 and JT5 wrist axes are driven through toothed timing belts whose tension must be checked every 6000 operating hours. Measure tension using a sonic belt tension meter and adjust the idler until the reading falls within 180 to 220 Hz for the standard belt fitted to these axes. A belt that is too loose will skip teeth under peak acceleration and cause a sudden unrecoverable position error, while an overtightened belt overloads the motor bearing. Always release servo power and engage the mechanical support before slackening the idler lock bolts. After adjustment, rotate the axis through several full cycles and re-measure, as the tension settles once the belt seats. Replace any belt showing tooth root cracking, edge fraying, or visible tension member exposure.

chunks.title: Lubrication of the linear slider ball screw and guide rails
chunks.text: Robots supplied on a traversing slider unit require separate lubrication of the ball screw and the linear guide blocks. Apply lithium grease of consistency NLGI 2 through the grease nipple on each guide block every 500 operating hours or every three months. The ball screw is lubricated through a central manifold and requires a measured charge rather than pumping until resistance is felt. Wipe the exposed rail surfaces before greasing so that abrasive particles are not carried into the recirculating ball tracks. Bellows covers must be inspected for tears, as a breached bellows admits swarf that will destroy a guide block within weeks. A dry or contaminated slider announces itself as a rising motor current on the traverse axis and an audible grinding at low speed.

chunks.title: JMOVE and LMOVE motion statements in AS language
chunks.text: The AS language provides JMOVE for joint interpolated motion and LMOVE for linear interpolated motion to a taught pose. JMOVE drives all axes to arrive simultaneously without regard to the path traced by the tool centre point, making it the faster choice for free space transitions. LMOVE constrains the tool centre point to a straight line, which is required when entering or leaving a fixture or when following a process path. Speed is set by the preceding SPEED instruction and accuracy by the ACCURACY instruction, both of which remain in effect until changed. Use the ACCURACY value to permit corner rounding between consecutive segments and reduce cycle time. A LMOVE that cannot be executed without passing through a singularity will abort with a motion error rather than silently deviating from the line.
chunks.query: JMOVE and LMOVE motion statements in AS language

chunks.title: Jogging in base frame versus tool frame
chunks.text: The teach pendant offers jogging in joint mode, base coordinate mode, and tool coordinate mode, selected with the coordinate key. In base mode the jog keys translate the tool centre point along the fixed axes of the robot base regardless of wrist orientation. In tool mode the same keys translate along the axes of the currently active tool frame, so the direction of travel rotates as the wrist rotates. Tool mode is the natural choice when approaching a workpiece along the axis of a gripper or a dispensing nozzle. Confirm which tool number is active before jogging, because an incorrect tool definition sends the arm in an unexpected direction. Joint mode remains available for recovering from near-singular poses where cartesian jogging becomes ill-conditioned.

chunks.text_ko: 티치 펜던트는 좌표계 키로 선택할 수 있는 관절 모드, 베이스 좌표 모드, 툴 좌표 모드의 조그 기능을 제공합니다. 베이스 모드에서는 손목 자세와 관계없이 로봇 베이스의 고정된 축을 따라 툴 센터 포인트가 이동합니다. 툴 모드에서는 동일한 키가 현재 활성화된 공구 좌표계의 축을 따라 이동시키므로 손목이 회전하면 이동 방향도 함께 회전합니다. 그리퍼나 디스펜싱 노즐의 축 방향을 따라 공작물에 접근할 때는 툴 모드가 자연스러운 선택입니다. 공구 정의가 잘못되면 예상치 못한 방향으로 암이 움직이므로 조그 전에 활성 공구 번호를 반드시 확인하십시오. 직교 조그가 불안정해지는 특이점 부근 자세에서 복구할 때는 관절 모드를 사용할 수 있습니다.

chunks.title: Five-point tool centre point calibration
chunks.text: Tool centre point calibration is performed by touching a fixed reference tip from five distinct approach orientations and recording each pose. The controller solves for the translation between the flange origin and the tool tip that best satisfies all five observations. Spread the orientations as widely as the workcell permits, since clustered poses produce an ill-conditioned solution and a large residual. The reported residual error should be below 0.5 mm; a larger value indicates either a slipped reference tip or insufficient orientation diversity. Tool orientation, as distinct from position, is taught separately by aligning the tool axes with a known reference frame. Recalibrate whenever the end effector is removed and refitted, even if it is bolted to the same dowelled interface.

chunks.title: Registering payload mass and inertia
chunks.text: The controller requires the mass, centre of gravity offset, and moment of inertia of the end effector plus workpiece to plan motion correctly. These values are entered in the tool registration screen and may be switched at run time when the robot picks and places parts of different mass. An underdeclared payload causes overshoot, path deviation on fast moves, and eventual overload alarms on the wrist axes. An overdeclared payload is conservative for safety but reduces achievable acceleration and lengthens cycle time unnecessarily. The centre of gravity offset matters as much as the mass itself, because a light tool on a long extension produces a large inertial moment. Where the inertia is unknown, use the automatic payload estimation routine rather than guessing.

chunks.title: Software travel limits and interference zone definition
chunks.text: Software travel limits restrict each joint to a range narrower than the mechanical stopper positions and are checked by the motion planner before every segment. Interference zones define cuboid regions in the base coordinate system that the tool centre point may not enter, or alternatively must not leave. Zones can be linked to a digital signal so that a neighbouring machine can grant or deny access to a shared volume, preventing two arms from occupying the same space. Note that a standard interference zone is enforced by the motion planner and is not a safety-rated function; safety-rated space limiting requires the dedicated safety unit. Define zones with a margin that accounts for the physical envelope of the end effector, not just the tool centre point. Test each zone by deliberately jogging toward the boundary at low speed and confirming the stop occurs where expected.

chunks.title: Configuring the controller as a PROFINET IO device
chunks.text: The optional fieldbus board allows the E controller to participate in a PROFINET network as an IO device under a supervising controller. Import the supplied GSDML file into the engineering tool of the line controller to make the device type available in the hardware catalogue. Assign a unique device name, as PROFINET resolves stations by name rather than by IP address at startup. The input and output sizes are configured in fixed-length byte arrays that must match on both ends or the connection will be refused with a configuration mismatch. Map the robot signal numbers to the exchanged bytes in the fieldbus configuration screen on the pendant. Cycle the controller power after changing the byte layout, since the mapping is read only at initialisation.

chunks.title: EtherNet/IP implicit and explicit messaging modes
chunks.text: The EtherNet/IP interface supports both implicit cyclic messaging for time-critical I/O and explicit messaging for acyclic parameter access. Implicit messaging establishes a connection with a requested packet interval, typically between 8 and 32 milliseconds depending on the number of connected devices. Explicit messaging uses unconnected requests to read or write specific object attributes and is appropriate for recipe download or diagnostic polling. Do not use explicit messaging inside a fast production loop, as the response time is not deterministic and will vary with network load. The consumed and produced assembly instance numbers must match the values configured in the scanner. Monitor the connection timeout counter during commissioning to confirm the requested packet interval is sustainable on your network.

chunks.title: Setting the controller IP address and subnet mask
chunks.text: The controller network settings are reached through the auxiliary function menu on the teach pendant under the network configuration entry. Enter the IP address, subnet mask, and default gateway using the numeric keypad, then save and restart the controller for the change to take effect. The factory default address is 192.168.0.2 with a subnet mask of 255.255.255.0. Ensure the address does not collide with another station, as a duplicate address produces intermittent communication loss that is easily mistaken for a cable fault. The service port on the front panel operates on a separate fixed subnet reserved for maintenance laptops and is not routable to the plant network. Record the assigned address on the cabinet label for future service visits.

chunks.title: Fieldbus watchdog timeout and safe state on connection loss
chunks.text: The fieldbus interface maintains a watchdog timer that is refreshed by each successfully received cyclic frame from the supervising controller. If no frame arrives within the configured watchdog period, the interface declares the connection lost and drives all received signals to a defined fallback state. The fallback behaviour is selectable between holding the last received value and clearing all inputs to zero, and the choice has direct safety consequences for the cell logic. Holding last value can leave a start command latched true, causing the robot to continue cycling after the line controller has stopped. Set the watchdog period to at least three times the requested packet interval to avoid nuisance trips on a busy network. Test the configured behaviour by physically unplugging the network cable during a dry run.

chunks.title: Remote terminal access for program transfer and monitoring
chunks.text: The controller exposes a terminal service over TCP that accepts the same command set available at the pendant, allowing program listing, variable inspection, and file transfer from a connected laptop. Authentication is limited, so the service should be reachable only from a maintenance VLAN and never exposed to a routable plant network. Program files are transferred as plain text and may be archived to a version control system for change tracking. Take care when writing variables through the terminal while the robot is in automatic mode, as there is no interlock preventing a change to a value that motion is currently using. Close the session cleanly, since an abandoned connection occupies one of a small number of available sockets. Disable the service entirely on installations where remote access is not required.

chunks.title: Mastering the robot using the calibration jig
chunks.text: Mastering establishes the correspondence between the absolute encoder reading and the mechanical zero position of each axis. The procedure uses a calibration jig that locates against machined witness surfaces on the arm, positioning the axis precisely at its reference angle. With the jig fitted, execute the mastering command for the selected axis and the controller records the current encoder count as the zero reference. Perform mastering with the arm at ambient temperature, as thermal growth in the links introduces a measurable offset when the machine is hot. Master the axes in the order given in the manual, since the reference position of the wrist axes depends on the main axes already being correct. Save the resulting mastering data to external media immediately, as recovering it later requires repeating the entire procedure.

chunks.text_ko: 마스터링은 절대 엔코더 값과 각 축의 기계적 원점 위치 사이의 대응 관계를 설정하는 작업입니다. 이 절차에서는 암의 가공된 기준면에 밀착되는 교정 지그를 사용하여 축을 기준 각도에 정확히 위치시킵니다. 지그를 장착한 상태에서 해당 축의 마스터링 명령을 실행하면 컨트롤러가 현재 엔코더 값을 원점 기준으로 기록합니다. 링크의 열팽창이 측정 가능한 오프셋을 유발하므로 반드시 상온 상태에서 마스터링을 수행하십시오. 손목 축의 기준 위치는 주축이 먼저 정확해야 성립하므로 설명서에 제시된 순서대로 축을 마스터링하십시오. 결과 데이터를 즉시 외부 매체에 저장하십시오. 나중에 복구하려면 전체 절차를 다시 수행해야 합니다.

chunks.title: Recovering reference position after loss of absolute data
chunks.text: If the backup cells are exhausted or disconnected while the controller is powered down, the absolute count is lost and every affected axis reports a position undefined condition. Recovery requires re-establishing the reference for each axis before any programmed motion can be executed. Where a full jig procedure is impractical, a single-axis quick reference can be performed by jogging to the witness marks scribed on the casting and confirming the position. This quick method restores approximate correspondence sufficient for the arm to reach a stored pose, after which a full procedure should be scheduled. All taught program positions remain valid in joint coordinates but will be physically wrong until the reference is restored. Never attempt to run production on quick-referenced axes, as the accumulated error can drive the tool into a fixture.

chunks.title: Adjusting mechanical stopper positions to restrict axis travel
chunks.text: Adjustable mechanical stoppers are available on the first three axes to physically restrict the working envelope where the cell layout demands it. The stopper block is repositioned into one of the tapped hole sets on the casting and secured with the specified bolts at the stated torque. Mechanical stoppers must always be set outside the corresponding software limit so that the software boundary is reached first under normal operation. The stopper is a last-resort energy-absorbing device sized for a single high-speed impact and must be replaced after any collision that contacts it. Restricting the envelope mechanically is the only measure recognised for reducing the required guarded area in some jurisdictions. Record the fitted stopper positions in the cell risk assessment documentation.

chunks.title: Reducing cycle time through acceleration and corner rounding
chunks.text: Cycle time is most effectively reduced by relaxing path accuracy at corners rather than by raising the commanded speed on straight segments. Increasing the accuracy value permits the planner to round the corner and carry velocity through the transition instead of decelerating to a stop at each taught point. Review the taught path for redundant intermediate points, which force unnecessary decelerations and add no value to the trajectory. Verify the declared payload is not overstated, since a conservative payload figure caps the acceleration the planner is willing to command. Where the arm is clearly not saturating its torque limits, the acceleration override can be raised in steps while monitoring peak current on each axis. Always confirm the resulting path still clears fixtures, since corner rounding cuts inside the taught geometry.

chunks.title: Suppressing residual oscillation at the end of a move
chunks.text: Residual oscillation appearing as the arm settles at the end of a rapid move is normally caused by the excitation of a lightly damped structural mode by the deceleration transient. The controller provides a notch filter in the velocity loop that can be tuned to the offending frequency to remove the excitation energy. Determine the frequency by capturing the torque command trace during settling and reading the period of the decaying ringing. Excessive velocity loop gain will also produce ringing, in which case reducing the gain is the correct action rather than adding a filter. Note that this differs from a low-frequency sway of the entire machine, which points to the supporting structure rather than the servo tuning. Confirm any tuning change across the full payload range, since the resonant frequency shifts with the mass carried.

chunks.text_ko: 급속 이동이 끝나고 암이 정지할 때 나타나는 잔류 진동은 일반적으로 감속 과도 응답이 감쇠가 약한 구조 모드를 여기시켜 발생합니다. 컨트롤러는 속도 루프에 노치 필터를 제공하므로 해당 주파수에 맞추어 여기 에너지를 제거할 수 있습니다. 정정 중 토크 지령 파형을 캡처하여 감쇠 진동의 주기를 읽으면 주파수를 확인할 수 있습니다. 속도 루프 게인이 과도해도 진동이 발생하며, 이 경우에는 필터를 추가하는 것이 아니라 게인을 낮추는 것이 올바른 조치입니다. 이는 기계 전체가 낮은 주파수로 흔들리는 현상과는 다르며, 후자는 서보 튜닝이 아니라 지지 구조물의 문제를 시사합니다. 반송 질량에 따라 공진 주파수가 이동하므로 튜닝 변경 후에는 전체 페이로드 범위에서 확인하십시오.

chunks.title: Base mounting bolt pattern and torque for the M1013 cobot
chunks.text: The M1013 base is secured with four M8 bolts of property class 8.8 arranged on a 132 mm pitch circle diameter. Tighten each bolt to 20 N-m using a calibrated torque wrench in a crosswise pattern. Two dowel pins of 6 mm diameter locate the base against the mounting plate and must be fitted to guarantee repeatable relocation after removal. The mounting surface must support a static load of at least four times the combined robot and payload weight, accounting for the dynamic reaction moment during rapid deceleration. Mounting to a bench top thinner than 15 mm steel or an unbraced aluminium extrusion frame is not permitted. Re-torque the bolts after the first week of operation.
chunks.query: M8 bolt torque 20 N-m and 132 mm pitch circle for the M1013 base
chunks.text_ko: M1013 베이스는 132 mm 피치 원 직경에 배치된 재질 등급 8.8의 M8 볼트 4개로 고정합니다. 교정된 토크 렌치를 사용하여 각 볼트를 대각선 패턴으로 20 N-m까지 조이십시오. 직경 6 mm 다웰 핀 2개가 베이스를 장착 플레이트에 위치시키며, 탈거 후 반복 재설치 정밀도를 보장하려면 반드시 장착해야 합니다. 장착면은 급속 감속 시 발생하는 동적 반력 모멘트를 고려하여 로봇과 페이로드 합계 중량의 최소 4배에 해당하는 정적 하중을 지지해야 합니다. 두께 15 mm 미만의 강재 작업대나 보강되지 않은 알루미늄 프로파일 프레임에는 설치할 수 없습니다. 운전 첫 주 경과 후 볼트를 재체결하십시오.
chunks.query_ko: M1013 베이스 M8 볼트 20 N-m 토크와 132 mm 피치 원

chunks.title: Mounting orientation and tilt angle configuration
chunks.text: The cobot may be installed on a floor, wall, ceiling, or an arbitrary tilted surface, but the installation angle must be entered during the initial setup. The controller uses this angle to compute the gravity vector acting on each link for both motion planning and collision detection. An incorrect installation angle causes the collision detection algorithm to interpret the constant gravity torque as an external force, producing spurious protective stops during normal motion. Enter the tilt as two angles describing the rotation of the base plane relative to horizontal. The setup screen provides an automatic measurement option that uses the internal accelerometer to determine the angle. Re-run the measurement whenever the robot is relocated or the mounting surface is modified.
chunks.query: setting the installation angle when the cobot is not mounted on a flat floor

chunks.title: Workspace clearance and pedestal rigidity for collaborative operation
chunks.text: Provide sufficient clear space around the installed arm that an operator cannot be trapped between a moving link and a fixed structure. A minimum clearance of 500 mm is recommended between the reachable envelope and any wall, column, or adjacent machine where a person may stand. Pinch points created by the gap between the arm and a fixture are a common finding during collaborative risk assessment and often require the layout to be changed rather than the speed reduced. The supporting pedestal must not deflect appreciably under the reaction moment, because a compliant mount degrades the accuracy of the force estimation used for collision detection. A wobbling mount typically raises the noise floor of the joint torque signals and forces the sensitivity to be reduced. Verify stability by pushing the tool flange firmly and observing any movement at the base.
chunks.query: how much room should be left around the arm so nobody gets caught against a wall or fixture

chunks.title: Unpacking weight and two-person lifting requirement
chunks.text: The packaged manipulator weighs approximately 43 kg for the M1013 model and must be lifted by two people or with mechanical assistance. Lift the arm by the base casting and the upper link, never by the wrist or by an attached end effector. Keep the arm in its folded shipping pose until it is bolted down, since the extended arm shifts the centre of gravity well outside the base footprint. Do not remove the transport foam from between the links until the base is secured. The controller unit is packed separately and weighs approximately 15 kg. Inspect for shipping damage and photograph any crate damage before disposal in case a carrier claim is required.
chunks.query: how much does the arm weigh and can one person lift it out of the crate

chunks.title: Controller cabinet ventilation clearance and ingress protection
chunks.text: The control box requires a minimum free space of 100 mm on the intake and exhaust faces to sustain the designed airflow. Do not stand the unit on carpet, foam packing, or accumulated swarf, as these obstruct the underside intake. The control box carries an IP20 rating and must be housed in an additional enclosure where coolant mist, conductive dust, or washdown is present. Ambient temperature at the intake must remain between 0 and 50 degrees Celsius, with condensation avoided by keeping the unit powered during cold shutdown periods. Mounting the box inside a sealed cabinet without forced ventilation will raise the internal temperature beyond the rating even in a cool room. Check and clean the intake grille as part of the periodic inspection.
chunks.query: the control box sits in a sealed cupboard and keeps overheating even though the room is cool
chunks.text_ko: 컨트롤 박스는 설계된 공기 흐름을 유지하기 위해 흡기면과 배기면에 최소 100 mm의 여유 공간이 필요합니다. 카펫, 포장용 폼, 쌓인 절삭 칩 위에 본체를 올려놓지 마십시오. 하부 흡기구가 막힙니다. 컨트롤 박스는 IP20 등급이므로 절삭유 미스트, 전도성 분진, 물 세척이 있는 환경에서는 추가 외함에 수납해야 합니다. 흡기부 주위 온도는 섭씨 0도에서 50도 사이를 유지해야 하며, 한랭 정지 기간에도 전원을 유지하여 결로를 방지하십시오. 강제 환기 없이 밀폐된 캐비닛 안에 본체를 설치하면 실내가 시원하더라도 내부 온도가 정격을 초과합니다. 정기 점검 시 흡기 그릴을 확인하고 청소하십시오.
chunks.query_ko: 제어 박스를 밀폐된 장 안에 넣어두었더니 실내는 시원한데 자꾸 과열됩니다

chunks.title: Control box mains input and 24 V internal supply
chunks.text: The control box accepts a single-phase supply of 100 to 240 V AC at 50 or 60 Hz and draws a maximum of 800 W for the M series. Protect the circuit with a 10 A breaker and provide a dedicated protective earth conductor to the labelled stud on the rear panel. The internal 24 V DC supply is available at the user terminal block and can source up to 2 A total for customer devices. Exceeding the 2 A budget causes the supply to fold back, which presents as apparently random resets of connected sensors rather than an explicit fault. Where the end effector requires more current, provide a separate external supply and bond its zero volt reference to the controller zero volt terminal. Never back-feed an external 24 V supply into the internal supply terminals.
chunks.query: 100 to 240 V AC single-phase input and the 2 A limit on the internal 24 V supply
chunks.text_ko: 컨트롤 박스는 50 또는 60 Hz의 단상 100에서 240 V AC 전원을 입력받으며 M 시리즈 기준 최대 800 W를 소비합니다. 회로는 10 A 차단기로 보호하고 후면 패널의 표시된 스터드에 전용 보호 접지 도체를 연결하십시오. 내부 24 V DC 전원은 사용자 단자대에서 사용할 수 있으며 고객 장치에 합계 2 A까지 공급할 수 있습니다. 2 A 예산을 초과하면 전원이 폴드백되어 명시적인 결함 없이 연결된 센서가 무작위로 리셋되는 것처럼 보입니다. 엔드 이펙터에 더 큰 전류가 필요한 경우 별도의 외부 전원을 공급하고 그 0 V 기준을 컨트롤러 0 V 단자에 본딩하십시오. 외부 24 V 전원을 내부 전원 단자로 역급전하지 마십시오.
chunks.query_ko: 단상 100에서 240 V AC 입력과 내부 24 V 전원의 2 A 제한

chunks.title: Tool flange connector pin assignment
chunks.text: The tool flange carries an eight-pin connector providing power and I/O to the end effector. Pin 1 is zero volts and pin 2 supplies tool power, selectable between 12 V and 24 V in the software configuration. Pins 3 and 4 are digital outputs rated at 1 A each, pins 5 and 6 are digital inputs, and pins 7 and 8 are analog inputs configurable for either voltage or current mode. Set the tool voltage before connecting the gripper, since applying 24 V to a 12 V device will damage it immediately on power-up. The analog input mode is selected in software and a mismatch between the configured mode and the wired sensor produces a reading pinned at zero or full scale. Total tool current is limited to 2 A across all pins combined.
chunks.query: tool flange eight-pin connector pin assignment and 12 V or 24 V selection
chunks.text_ko: 툴 플랜지에는 엔드 이펙터에 전원과 입출력을 공급하는 8핀 커넥터가 있습니다. 1번 핀은 0 V이고 2번 핀은 공구 전원으로 소프트웨어 설정에서 12 V 또는 24 V 중 선택할 수 있습니다. 3번과 4번 핀은 각각 1 A 정격의 디지털 출력, 5번과 6번 핀은 디지털 입력, 7번과 8번 핀은 전압 또는 전류 모드로 설정 가능한 아날로그 입력입니다. 12 V 장치에 24 V를 인가하면 전원 투입 즉시 손상되므로 그리퍼를 연결하기 전에 공구 전압을 먼저 설정하십시오. 아날로그 입력 모드는 소프트웨어에서 선택하며 설정 모드와 배선된 센서가 일치하지 않으면 측정값이 0 또는 최대치에 고정됩니다. 전체 핀을 합한 공구 전류는 2 A로 제한됩니다.
chunks.query_ko: 툴 플랜지 8핀 커넥터 핀 배치와 12 V 24 V 선택

chunks.title: Electrostatic discharge precautions during service
chunks.text: Circuit boards inside the control box and the joint modules contain components that are damaged by static discharge at voltages well below the human perception threshold. Wear a grounded wrist strap connected to the chassis bonding point before opening any cover or handling a board. Store removed boards in conductive bags rather than on a bench surface, and never place them on foam packing that is not explicitly antistatic. Damage from a static event frequently does not cause immediate failure but instead weakens a junction, producing an intermittent fault weeks later that is impossible to trace to its cause. Discharge yourself before touching a connector even when only unplugging a cable. Low humidity in winter substantially increases the risk in most factory environments.
chunks.query: a board we swapped in last month started failing intermittently and we cannot find why

chunks.title: Routing and bend radius of the base to controller cable
chunks.text: The cable connecting the manipulator base to the control box must not be bent to a radius smaller than 80 mm at any point along its run. Do not coil surplus cable tightly; lay excess length in a wide loop or a figure-of-eight to avoid inducing a circulating field. The connector at the base end is keyed and secured with a threaded collar that must be tightened fully by hand until the seal compresses. Route the cable so that it cannot be walked on, run over by a pallet truck, or trapped by a closing guard door. Inspect the strain relief at both ends for jacket cracking during periodic maintenance. A damaged main cable presents as multiple simultaneous joint communication faults rather than a single joint error.
chunks.query: minimum bend radius for the cable between the arm base and the control box

chunks.title: Wiring external devices to the user I/O terminal block
chunks.text: The user terminal block inside the control box provides sixteen digital inputs and sixteen digital outputs for connection to peripheral equipment. Inputs are configurable as sinking or sourcing by moving the common jumper, and all inputs on a block share the same configuration. Outputs are transistor type rated at 500 mA per channel with a total block limit of 4 A. Inductive loads such as valve solenoids and contactor coils must be fitted with a flyback diode across the coil, otherwise the switching transient will progressively destroy the output transistor. Use ferrules on stranded conductors and torque the terminal screws to the value marked on the block. Label every wire at both ends, since an unlabelled loom makes future fault finding disproportionately expensive.
chunks.query: wiring valve solenoids to the digital outputs on the user terminal block

chunks.title: Speed and separation monitoring in collaborative operation
chunks.text: Speed and separation monitoring maintains a protective separation distance between the moving arm and the approaching operator, reducing robot speed as the distance closes. The required separation distance is calculated from the robot speed, the operator approach speed, the total system reaction time, and the stopping distance of the arm. External sensing such as a scanner or a safety camera provides the distance input, since the robot itself has no means of detecting an approaching person. When the calculated separation is violated the robot must stop before contact occurs, and it may resume automatically once the distance is restored. This mode allows higher productivity than power and force limiting because the arm can move at full speed while nobody is nearby. The stopping distance must be measured on the actual installed system rather than taken from a datasheet.
chunks.query: speed and separation monitoring protective distance calculation for collaborative operation

chunks.title: Power and force limiting with collision sensitivity levels
chunks.text: In power and force limiting mode the arm is permitted to contact an operator provided the resulting force and pressure remain below the biomechanical limits for the affected body region. Collision sensitivity is configured on a scale where a lower setting tolerates greater external force before triggering a protective stop. Setting the sensitivity too low to stop nuisance trips defeats the protective measure and invalidates the collaborative risk assessment. Sensitivity must be validated by measurement with a calibrated force and pressure gauge at every location where contact is credible. Transient and quasi-static contact have different permitted limits, and a clamping scenario against a fixture is far more demanding than a free impact. Record the measured values against the configured sensitivity in the validation report.
chunks.query: collision sensitivity levels and biomechanical force limits in power and force limiting mode

chunks.title: Dual-channel safety input wiring for protective stop
chunks.text: The safety I/O connector provides dual-channel inputs for emergency stop, protective stop, and safeguard reset functions. Each function occupies two independent channels that are cross monitored, and both must open together for a valid request. A discrepancy between channels persisting beyond the tolerance time latches a fault that requires a deliberate reset rather than clearing itself. Protective stop performs a category 2 stop in which servo power is maintained and the arm holds position under control, whereas emergency stop removes drive power. Automatic restart after a protective stop is permitted only where the risk assessment supports it and a reset device is positioned with full view of the working area. Test each channel individually during commissioning.
chunks.query: dual-channel protective stop and emergency stop safety input wiring

chunks.title: Defining safety zones and virtual boundaries
chunks.text: Safety zones are configured as planes or boxes in the workspace and are monitored by the safety controller independently of the motion program. A protected zone may be defined as a region the tool must not enter, or as a boundary the arm must remain within. Each zone can carry its own speed limit, so the arm may be allowed to enter a shared area only at reduced velocity. Zone monitoring accounts for the declared tool dimensions, so an accurate tool model must be entered or the physical gripper will cross the boundary before the monitored point does. Changes to zone definitions require the safety configuration to be re-applied and confirmed with a password, and the resulting checksum should be recorded. Validate every zone physically by jogging toward the boundary at low speed.
chunks.query: setting up a virtual boundary the arm is not allowed to cross

chunks.title: Transition between full speed and reduced speed states
chunks.text: The cell may be configured to operate at full productive speed while the working area is clear, and to drop to a reduced velocity when a person is detected within the outer sensing field. The transition must complete before the person can reach the hazard zone, which constrains how far out the outer field must be placed. Calculate the required detection distance from the stopping performance of the arm plus the reaction time of the sensing chain, not merely from the walking speed of an average adult. The changeover itself must be monitored by the safety controller so that a failure to reduce speed is detected and forces a stop. Operators frequently report that the cell feels slow because the outer field is oversized, but reducing it without recalculating is not permissible. Verify the actual achieved speed after transition with a measuring device rather than trusting the displayed value.
chunks.query: the cell drops to a crawl as soon as anyone walks near it and production is suffering

chunks.title: Joint torque deviation and collision detection trip
chunks.text: A joint torque deviation error is raised when the measured joint torque differs from the value predicted by the dynamic model by more than the configured threshold. The dynamic model accounts for gravity, inertia, friction, and the declared payload, so an error in any of these inputs produces a false trip. The most common cause of repeated nuisance trips is an incorrect payload or tool centre of gravity entry rather than an actual collision. Friction rises when a joint is cold, so trips concentrated in the first minutes of a shift point to the friction model rather than to a mechanical fault. Review the torque trace captured at the moment of the trip to distinguish a genuine impact, which shows a sharp step, from a modelling error, which shows a slow divergence. Increasing the threshold to suppress the symptom is acceptable only after the root cause has been excluded.
chunks.query: joint torque deviation error and collision detection threshold trips

chunks.title: Servo remains disabled after clearing an emergency stop
chunks.text: After an emergency stop device is released, the drive stage is not re-energised automatically because an unattended restart would be hazardous. The recovery sequence requires the stop condition to be physically cleared, a reset to be issued, and then servo power to be re-enabled from the pendant or the configured reset input. If servo power still cannot be established, one of the parallel stop sources is very likely still open, since all sources are combined in series. Check the physical stop buttons, the safety I/O terminals, the teach pendant connection, and any external safety controller contribution in turn. The status screen shows the state of each contributing source and should be consulted before any measurement is taken. A stop button left latched at a remote station is the single most common cause.
chunks.query: we released the mushroom button and reset it but the drives still will not come alive

chunks.title: Joint module over-temperature warning
chunks.text: Each joint module monitors its internal temperature and issues a warning when the motor winding or the drive electronics approach their limits. The arm continues to operate through the warning but will initiate a controlled stop if the temperature continues to rise to the shutdown threshold. High duty cycles with heavy payloads and short dwell times give the joints little opportunity to shed heat, particularly on the shoulder joint which carries the greatest static load. Check whether the program holds the arm in a stationary outstretched pose for extended periods, since static holding torque generates heat without any motion. Ambient temperature at the installation and any radiant heat from nearby process equipment contribute directly. Adding a short retreat to a folded pose during idle periods substantially reduces the thermal load.
chunks.query: the shoulder joint keeps flagging a temperature warning during long cycles
chunks.text_ko: 각 관절 모듈은 내부 온도를 감시하여 모터 권선이나 구동 전자부가 한계에 접근하면 경고를 발령합니다. 경고 상태에서도 로봇은 계속 동작하지만 온도가 셧다운 임계값까지 상승하면 제어된 정지를 개시합니다. 무거운 페이로드와 짧은 정지 시간을 동반한 높은 가동률에서는 관절이 열을 방출할 여유가 부족하며, 특히 정적 하중이 가장 큰 어깨 관절에서 두드러집니다. 정지 상태의 유지 토크는 동작 없이도 열을 발생시키므로 프로그램이 암을 펼친 자세로 장시간 유지하는지 확인하십시오. 설치 장소의 주위 온도와 인근 공정 장비의 복사열도 직접적으로 영향을 미칩니다. 유휴 시간 동안 접힌 자세로 잠시 후퇴시키는 동작을 추가하면 열 부하가 크게 감소합니다.
chunks.query_ko: 긴 사이클 작업 중 어깨 관절에서 온도 경고가 계속 발생합니다

chunks.title: Joint identification mismatch after module replacement
chunks.text: Each joint module stores its own identity and calibration data, and the controller verifies that the modules present on the internal bus match the expected configuration at every startup. Fitting a replacement module without running the registration procedure produces a joint identification mismatch error that blocks servo enable. The registration procedure writes the joint index and the arm serial number into the new module and imports its factory calibration constants. Do not swap modules between arms as a diagnostic shortcut without re-registering, because the stored calibration is specific to the module and not to the position. After registration, the affected joint must be re-zeroed before the arm will achieve its rated accuracy. Record the module serial numbers in the maintenance log for traceability.
chunks.query: joint identification mismatch error after replacing a joint module
chunks.text_ko: 각 관절 모듈은 자체 식별 정보와 교정 데이터를 저장하며 컨트롤러는 매 기동 시 내부 버스에 존재하는 모듈이 예상 구성과 일치하는지 검증합니다. 등록 절차를 수행하지 않고 교체 모듈을 장착하면 관절 식별 불일치 오류가 발생하여 서보 인에이블이 차단됩니다. 등록 절차는 새 모듈에 관절 번호와 로봇 일련번호를 기록하고 공장 교정 상수를 가져옵니다. 저장된 교정값은 장착 위치가 아니라 모듈 고유의 값이므로 재등록 없이 진단 목적으로 모듈을 다른 로봇과 교환하지 마십시오. 등록 후에는 해당 관절의 원점을 다시 설정해야 정격 정밀도를 확보할 수 있습니다. 추적성을 위해 모듈 일련번호를 유지보수 일지에 기록하십시오.
chunks.query_ko: 관절 모듈 교체 후 발생하는 관절 식별 불일치 오류

chunks.title: Loss of connection between the programming environment and the controller
chunks.text: The programming environment communicates with the control box over TCP, and a dropped session leaves the editor showing stale data while the robot continues to run its loaded program. Confirm the physical link and the assigned addresses first, then verify that no second client is already holding the single permitted engineering connection. A laptop that has switched to a wireless network while still cabled will often route the traffic out of the wrong interface. Firewall software on the laptop is a frequent cause on newly imaged machines and should be tested by temporarily disabling it. Note that losing the engineering connection does not stop the robot, which is deliberate but surprising to new users. Reconnect and re-read the program from the controller rather than pushing the possibly stale editor copy back down.

chunks.title: Joint module service life and wear indicators
chunks.text: Joint modules are specified for a nominal service life of 35000 operating hours under rated load and duty. Actual life depends strongly on the applied torque profile, and a joint that spends its cycle near the peak torque limit will wear considerably faster than the nominal figure suggests. Early indicators of wear include a rising friction estimate reported by the controller, increased audible noise at low speed, and a gradual increase in the residual position error after settling. The controller maintains a cumulative load counter per joint that should be reviewed at every annual inspection. Replace a module before failure where the cell has no tolerance for unplanned downtime, since a failed joint requires the arm to be taken out of service. Order replacements against the arm serial number to ensure the correct variant is supplied.

chunks.title: Cleaning and wipe-down for food and pharmaceutical applications
chunks.text: The standard arm carries an IP54 rating on the joints and tolerates wipe-down with a damp cloth and mild detergent. High-pressure washing, steam cleaning, and immersion are not permitted at this rating and will drive water past the joint seals. Isopropyl alcohol is acceptable for disinfection but repeated application will craze some plastic covers over time, so verify compatibility with the covers fitted. Avoid chlorinated cleaners on anodised surfaces, which cause pitting that then traps contamination. For applications requiring frequent aggressive cleaning, specify the variant with the higher ingress rating or fit a protective sleeve. Inspect all seals and cover joints for lifting or damage after each cleaning cycle.

chunks.title: Controller firmware update procedure
chunks.text: Firmware updates are applied from the programming environment or from a USB device inserted into the control box, and must not be interrupted once started. Back up the full robot configuration including programs, safety settings, and calibration data before beginning the update. The safety configuration is checked after the update and may require re-confirmation with a password, and in some releases a full revalidation of the safety functions is mandated. Verify the release notes for any change to default parameter values, since a changed default can alter cell behaviour on the first cycle after the update. Do not update firmware immediately before a production run without a validation window. Power interruption during the update can leave the controller in a state that requires factory recovery.

chunks.title: Backup and restore of the complete robot configuration
chunks.text: A complete backup comprises the user programs, the tool and workcell frame definitions, the safety configuration, the network settings, and the per-joint calibration data. Export the backup to external media at commissioning, after every significant program change, and before any firmware update. Store one copy off the machine and one with the cell documentation, since a backup held only on the controller is lost with the controller. Restoring to a replacement control box will not restore joint calibration if the arm itself is unchanged, because calibration lives in the joint modules rather than the controller. Verify a backup by restoring it to a spare unit rather than assuming the archive is readable. Label each archive with the date, the firmware version, and the cell identifier.

chunks.title: Periodic inspection schedule and record keeping
chunks.text: A documented inspection at defined intervals is required both by the manufacturer and by most machinery safety regulations. Daily checks cover the emergency stop function, visible cable damage, and any unusual noise or vibration reported by the operator. Monthly checks add bolt torque verification, cleaning of ventilation paths, and a review of the fault history for recurring entries. Annual checks include full verification of every safety function against the validation report, measurement of stopping distance, and review of the cumulative joint load counters. Records must be retained and made available during an audit, and an undocumented inspection is treated as an inspection that did not happen. Assign the responsibility to a named person rather than to a department.

chunks.title: DRL movej and movel motion commands
chunks.text: The Doosan Robot Language provides movej for joint space motion and movel for linear cartesian motion. The movej command accepts either a joint posture or a task pose and drives the axes to arrive together, giving the fastest transit through free space. The movel command holds the tool centre point on a straight line and is required for insertion, extraction, and process paths. Both commands accept velocity and acceleration arguments, and omitting them applies the global defaults set earlier in the program. The radius argument enables blending into the following motion, allowing the arm to carry speed through a corner instead of stopping at the point. A movel target that would require passing through a wrist singularity raises a motion error rather than deviating silently.

chunks.title: Hand guiding the arm to teach positions
chunks.text: Direct teaching allows an operator to grasp the arm and physically move it to the desired pose while the controller compensates for gravity and friction. Engage the mode with the button on the wrist and the arm becomes compliant, holding position when released. The quality of the experience depends entirely on an accurate payload and centre of gravity declaration, because the controller must cancel exactly the gravity torque and no more. An arm that drifts downward when released is under-compensated, while an arm that creeps upward is over-compensated, and both point to the payload entry rather than to a hardware fault. Compliance can be restricted to selected axes so that the arm can be guided along a plane while other directions stay locked. Positions captured this way should be refined numerically for tasks requiring high accuracy.

chunks.title: Tool centre point and payload setup wizard
chunks.text: The setup wizard guides the user through defining the tool centre point offset, the tool orientation, and the payload properties for each end effector. The tool centre point is established either by entering measured offsets from the flange or by touching a fixed reference point from several orientations. Payload mass, centre of gravity, and inertia may be entered from the gripper datasheet or determined by the automatic estimation routine. Multiple tool configurations can be stored and switched at run time, which is necessary when the arm uses a tool changer or handles parts of varying mass. An inaccurate tool definition affects motion accuracy, collision detection sensitivity, and safety zone monitoring simultaneously. Re-run the wizard whenever the end effector or the handled part changes significantly.

chunks.title: Defining workcell coordinate frames
chunks.text: A user coordinate frame lets positions be expressed relative to a fixture rather than to the robot base, so that a fixture that is moved requires only the frame to be redefined. Frames are taught by touching three points defining the origin and the direction of two axes. When a fixture is repositioned during a line change, redefining the frame shifts every position taught within it, avoiding the need to re-teach the whole program. Keep frames hierarchical where possible so that a pallet frame is defined relative to a table frame rather than to the base. Document which frame each routine uses, since a program executed against the wrong active frame will move to a plausible but incorrect location. Verify a redefined frame by running the program at reduced speed before returning to production.

chunks.title: Force controlled insertion and compliance
chunks.text: Force control allows the arm to regulate the contact force along selected directions while position control is maintained in the remaining directions. This is used for insertion tasks where the clearance is smaller than the accumulated positional uncertainty of the fixture and the part. Configure the compliant directions, the target force, and the maximum permitted deviation before entering the compliance block in the program. A spiral or wiggle search pattern superimposed on the insertion axis substantially improves the success rate when the hole location is uncertain. Set a timeout and a retreat action so a failed insertion does not stall the cycle indefinitely. Force estimation is derived from joint torques rather than a wrist sensor on the standard arm, so accuracy degrades near singular configurations.

chunks.title: Modbus TCP master and slave configuration
chunks.text: The controller can act as a Modbus TCP slave exposing its I/O and status registers, and simultaneously as a master polling external devices. Register addressing follows the standard convention, and an off-by-one error between zero-based and one-based numbering is the most frequent commissioning problem. Configure the polling interval for master connections with regard to the response time of the slave device, as an aggressive interval on a slow device fills the queue and delays other traffic. Connection loss to a polled slave should be handled explicitly in the program rather than allowing the last read value to persist silently. Modbus TCP provides no authentication, so the interface should be restricted to the cell network. Document the full register map alongside the cell drawings.

chunks.title: PROFINET communication module installation
chunks.text: PROFINET connectivity is provided by an optional module fitted into the expansion slot of the control box. Install the module with the controller fully powered down and confirm it is recognised in the device list before attempting configuration. Import the supplied GSDML file into the line controller engineering tool and assign a device name that matches the name written to the module. The exchanged data size is fixed by the selected module configuration and must agree at both ends or the connection is refused. Signal mapping between the PROFINET byte array and the robot I/O registers is configured in the controller user interface. Restart the controller after mapping changes so the configuration is read at initialisation.

chunks.title: Opening TCP sockets from a robot program
chunks.text: The robot language provides socket functions allowing a program to open a TCP connection to an external server and exchange arbitrary data. This is commonly used to request a part pose from a vision system or to report cycle results to a manufacturing execution system. Always set a receive timeout, since a blocking read against an unresponsive server will stall the program with no obvious indication at the pendant. Parse responses defensively and handle a malformed or truncated message rather than assuming a well-formed reply. Close sockets explicitly when finished, because a leaked socket accumulates until the connection pool is exhausted after many hours of running. Keep the protocol simple and text based so it can be tested independently with a terminal utility.

chunks.title: Static addressing versus DHCP for the control box
chunks.text: The control box network interface may be configured for a static address or to obtain one automatically from a server. A static address is strongly preferred for production installations because a changed address breaks every configured connection from supervisory systems. Where automatic assignment is used for convenience, reserve the address against the hardware address on the server so it does not change. The engineering interface and the fieldbus interface may occupy separate physical ports and separate subnets, and mixing them onto one flat network exposes cyclic traffic to broadcast interference. Verify that the configured gateway is correct if any remote access is required, since an absent gateway produces a connection that works locally and fails remotely. Record the addressing scheme in the cell documentation.

chunks.title: OPC UA server for supervisory data collection
chunks.text: The controller provides an OPC UA server exposing robot state, program status, and diagnostic counters to supervisory and analytics systems. Browsing the address space with a generic client is the fastest way to discover the available node identifiers during integration. Configure security with certificates and a named user rather than leaving the endpoint open with anonymous access. Subscription publishing intervals should be chosen to match the rate at which the consuming system can process updates, since an excessively fast subscription wastes controller resources without benefit. The server is intended for monitoring rather than for closed-loop control, and cyclic I/O should remain on the fieldbus. Note that the exposed node set may change between firmware versions, so pin the client to a tested version.

chunks.title: Initial setup wizard and joint zero position check
chunks.text: The initial setup wizard runs on first power-up and steps through language selection, installation angle entry, tool configuration, and a verification of each joint zero position. Joint zero is verified by driving each axis to its marked reference position and confirming the displayed angle reads zero within tolerance. A discrepancy indicates either a shipping disturbance or an incorrectly registered joint module and must be resolved before the arm is used. The wizard also prompts for the safety configuration, which must be completed and password protected before automatic operation is permitted. Do not skip the wizard by loading a configuration exported from a different arm, since calibration constants are arm specific. Record completion of the wizard in the commissioning documentation.

chunks.title: Gravity compensation calibration after mounting
chunks.text: The controller must know the direction of gravity relative to the base in order to compute the static torque required at each joint to hold a pose. This is derived from the declared installation angle, which is measured automatically using the internal accelerometer during the setup routine. Run the measurement with the arm stationary and the mounting fully bolted down, because a measurement taken on a temporary stand will not match the final installation. An error of only a few degrees produces a systematic torque offset that the collision detection interprets as a persistent external force. Symptoms include the arm drifting when compliance is engaged and protective stops that occur preferentially in one region of the workspace. Repeat the measurement after any change to the mounting.

chunks.title: Automatic payload estimation routine
chunks.text: Where the mass properties of an end effector are not known from a datasheet, the controller can determine them by executing a short prescribed motion and observing the resulting joint torques. Run the routine with the gripper in its normal working state and with any hoses or cables connected as they will be in production. The arm must have clear space for the estimation motion, which moves several joints through a moderate range at low speed. Results should be sanity checked against a weighed value where possible, as the estimation cannot distinguish payload mass from an unmodelled friction change. Re-run the routine whenever the tool is modified, including the addition of a camera bracket or a cable clamp. Store the resulting values in the tool configuration rather than leaving them only in the estimation screen.

chunks.title: Friction model identification for smooth low speed motion
chunks.text: Static and viscous friction in each joint are characterised during manufacture and stored as model parameters used by both motion control and external force estimation. Friction rises significantly when the mechanism is cold and falls as the joint reaches operating temperature, which is why some behaviours differ between the first cycle of a shift and steady running. A warm-up routine that exercises each axis through a moderate range for several minutes before production stabilises the behaviour. Where hand guiding feels notchy or the arm resists motion in one direction more than the other, the friction model may no longer match the mechanism. Re-identification is available in the service menu and should be performed after a joint module replacement. Persistent asymmetry after re-identification indicates mechanical damage rather than a modelling error.

chunks.title: Trading path accuracy against cycle time with blend radius
chunks.text: Specifying a blend radius on a motion command permits the planner to round the corner at the target point and carry velocity into the following segment. A larger radius yields a faster cycle but cuts further inside the taught geometry, so the resulting path must be checked for clearance against fixtures. A radius of zero forces the arm to come to rest at the point, which is necessary only where the process genuinely requires an exact stop such as a pick or a place. Many programs are slow simply because every taught point is a full stop, including intermediate via points that exist only to shape the path. Review the program for via points that can carry a generous blend and reserve exact stops for process points. Confirm any change by running the modified path at reduced speed with the fixtures in place.

chunks.title: S7-1500 rail mounting and clearance requirements
chunks.text: The SIMATIC S7-1500 modules mount on a dedicated profile rail that also serves as the backplane ground path. Maintain a clearance of 25 mm above and below the rail and 40 mm in front of the module faces for cabling and airflow. Modules must be installed contiguously from the CPU with no gaps, since the backplane bus is carried through the U connectors between adjacent modules. Install the rail horizontally wherever possible, because vertical installation requires the specified ambient temperature to be derated. Secure the rail at intervals appropriate to its length so that it cannot flex when modules are inserted. Fit the shield connection element at the bottom of the rail before wiring any analog or communication modules.
chunks.query: S7-1500 profile rail mounting clearance of 25 mm above and below
chunks.text_ko: SIMATIC S7-1500 모듈은 백플레인 접지 경로 역할도 겸하는 전용 프로파일 레일에 장착합니다. 레일 위아래로 25 mm, 모듈 전면으로 배선과 통풍을 위해 40 mm의 여유 공간을 확보하십시오. 백플레인 버스가 인접 모듈 사이의 U 커넥터를 통해 전달되므로 모듈은 CPU부터 빈 슬롯 없이 연속해서 설치해야 합니다. 수직 설치 시에는 규정된 주위 온도를 디레이팅해야 하므로 가능한 한 레일을 수평으로 설치하십시오. 모듈을 삽입할 때 휘지 않도록 레일 길이에 맞는 간격으로 고정하십시오. 아날로그 또는 통신 모듈을 배선하기 전에 레일 하단에 실드 접속 부품을 먼저 장착하십시오.

chunks.title: Cabinet thermal design and altitude derating
chunks.text: The permitted ambient temperature inside the enclosure is specified at the module intake rather than at the room, and the difference between the two can be substantial in a sealed cabinet. Above 2000 metres of installation altitude the maximum permitted ambient temperature must be reduced according to the derating table, because thinner air carries less heat away. The same derating applies to vertical rail installation and to installations with reduced clearance. Calculate the total dissipated power of all installed modules and compare it against the ability of the enclosure to reject that heat, adding forced ventilation or a cooling unit where required. Ignoring derating typically produces no immediate failure but shortens component life and causes unexplained faults years later. Position temperature-sensitive modules away from drive units and braking resistors.
chunks.query: the panel is installed at a mine site well above sea level and we are unsure what temperature limit applies
chunks.text_ko: 허용 주위 온도는 실내가 아니라 모듈 흡기부 기준으로 규정되며, 밀폐된 캐비닛에서는 두 값의 차이가 상당할 수 있습니다. 설치 고도 2000 미터를 초과하면 공기가 희박하여 열을 덜 운반하므로 디레이팅 표에 따라 최대 허용 주위 온도를 낮추어야 합니다. 동일한 디레이팅이 수직 레일 설치와 여유 공간이 축소된 설치에도 적용됩니다. 설치된 모든 모듈의 총 소비 전력을 계산하여 외함이 그 열을 방출할 수 있는 능력과 비교하고, 필요한 경우 강제 환기나 냉각 장치를 추가하십시오. 디레이팅을 무시하면 즉시 고장이 나지는 않지만 부품 수명이 단축되고 수년 후 원인 불명의 결함이 발생합니다. 온도에 민감한 모듈은 드라이브 유닛과 제동 저항기에서 떨어뜨려 배치하십시오.
