chunks.title: SINAMICS drive cabinet mounting and airflow
chunks.text: Drive units must be mounted vertically with the specified clear space above and below to allow the cooling airflow to pass through the heatsink channel. Do not mount a drive directly above a heat-generating component such as a braking resistor, since the upper unit will ingest preheated air. Where several drives are installed side by side, observe the lateral spacing given for the frame size rather than butting them together. The airflow path must be unobstructed by cable ducts or wiring looms crossing the intake or exhaust. Filter mats reduce the available airflow and their pressure drop must be included in the thermal calculation. Verify actual internal temperature with a datalogger over a full production shift rather than relying on a spot reading.
chunks.query: spacing and airflow clearance needed around drive units in the cabinet

chunks.title: Shield connection element installation for analog and bus cables
chunks.text: The shield connection element clamps onto the profile rail and provides a low impedance path from cable shields to the cabinet ground. Strip the cable jacket to expose the braid and clamp the braid directly under the terminal so that contact is made around the full circumference. A pigtail connection made by twisting the braid into a wire defeats the purpose, because the resulting inductance renders the shield ineffective at the frequencies that matter. Connect the shield of analog and communication cables at both ends unless a documented ground loop problem requires otherwise. The element must be bonded to the rail with the paint removed at the contact point. Fit the element before wiring, since retrofitting it requires the cables to be disturbed.
chunks.query: shield connection element clamping the cable braid to the profile rail

chunks.title: Grounding the profile rail and cabinet backplate
chunks.text: The profile rail must be bonded to the cabinet backplate and the backplate bonded to the plant protective earth with a conductor sized for the prospective fault current. Use serrated washers and remove paint or passivation at every bonding point so that the connection is metal to metal. The rail carries functional grounding for the module backplane in addition to protective earthing, so a poor rail bond produces both a safety hazard and erratic module behaviour. Bond cabinet doors to the backplate with a flexible braid rather than relying on the hinges. Where cabinets are bolted together, install equipotential bonding between adjacent backplates rather than trusting the mechanical joint. Verify all bonds with a low-resistance measurement during commissioning and record the values.
chunks.query: bonding the mounting rail and backplate to earth in the control cabinet

chunks.title: 24 V PELV supply and load power supply selection
chunks.text: The automation system requires a 24 V DC supply meeting the requirements for protective extra low voltage, with safe electrical separation from the mains circuit. Size the load power supply for the sum of all module currents plus a margin of at least 20 percent for inrush and future expansion. Separate the supply feeding the automation modules from the supply feeding inductive field devices, because coil switching transients propagate through a shared supply. The permitted voltage range is 20.4 to 28.8 V DC measured at the module terminals, not at the power supply output, so allow for volt drop in long runs. A supply that sags below the lower limit during a coincident inrush produces module resets that appear random. Use a supply with a buffering capability where brief mains interruptions are expected.
chunks.query: 24 V DC PELV supply and the 20.4 to 28.8 V permitted range at the module terminals

chunks.title: Motor cable shielding and EMC practice for SINAMICS drives
chunks.text: Motor cables between the drive and the motor must be shielded, with the shield bonded circumferentially at both the drive end and the motor terminal box. The switching output of the inverter produces steep voltage edges that radiate strongly from an unshielded or poorly terminated cable. Keep motor cables physically separated from signal, encoder, and network cabling, and cross at right angles where a crossing is unavoidable. Do not exceed the maximum permitted motor cable length for the frame size, as the cable capacitance loads the output stage and can cause overcurrent trips. Use the supplied shield clamps rather than cable ties over the braid. Poor motor cable practice is the most frequent single cause of unexplained communication faults elsewhere in the panel.
chunks.query: shielding and separation requirements for the cable running to the motor

chunks.title: Sinking and sourcing configuration of digital input modules
chunks.text: Digital input modules are supplied in variants for sinking or sourcing field wiring, and the two cannot be interchanged by rewiring alone. A sourcing input module expects the field device to supply 24 V to the input terminal, with the module common connected to zero volts. A sinking module expects the field device to pull the input to zero volts, with the module common connected to 24 V. Connecting a three-wire sensor of the wrong polarity type produces an input that reads permanently true or permanently false depending on the mismatch. Verify the sensor type marked on its body against the module variant before wiring the loom. Mixing types on a single module is not possible because the common is shared across the whole group.
chunks.query: sinking versus sourcing digital input module wiring for three-wire sensors

chunks.title: Analog signal integrity and reference potential
chunks.text: Analog measurement circuits are sensitive to potential differences between the sensor location and the module reference terminal. Where the sensor is grounded at a remote point, a difference of only a few volts between grounds drives a current through the signal return and appears directly as a measurement offset. Use isolated analog modules or a transmitter with galvanic separation where the sensor cannot be left floating. Route analog cables away from motor and switching circuits and terminate the shield at the shield element rather than at a terminal. Unused analog channels should be configured as deactivated rather than left enabled, since a floating input drifts and may trigger a wire-break diagnostic. A slow drifting reading that correlates with other equipment starting is nearly always a grounding problem rather than a faulty sensor.
chunks.query: the pressure reading creeps up whenever the big pump across the shop starts

chunks.title: Equipotential bonding between separated cabinets
chunks.text: Where parts of an installation are housed in cabinets separated by more than a few metres, an equipotential bonding conductor must be installed between them in addition to the protective earth. The bonding conductor carries the current that would otherwise flow through cable shields, and must have a cross section substantially larger than the shield it protects. Run the bonding conductor parallel to and close alongside the data cable rather than by a separate route, so that the enclosed loop area is minimised. Without bonding, the shield of a network cable becomes the unintended path for equalising current, which heats the braid and injects noise into the signal pair. Symptoms include communication errors that appear only when heavy plant equipment starts or stops. Fibre optic cable is an alternative where bonding across a long distance is impractical.
chunks.query: network errors between two panels at opposite ends of the building whenever big machinery kicks in

chunks.title: Fail-safe CPU and the PROFIsafe protocol
chunks.text: A fail-safe CPU executes both a standard user program and a separate safety program whose instructions are processed with additional diversity and comparison. Safety-related data travels over the same PROFINET network as standard data, protected by the PROFIsafe protocol layer which adds a consecutive number, a timeout, an identifier, and a cyclic redundancy check. This black channel principle means the underlying network requires no safety approval, because a corrupted or delayed message is detected by the protocol rather than prevented by the medium. Each fail-safe device is assigned a unique PROFIsafe address that must match between the hardware configuration and the switch or dial setting on the device. A duplicated address is a serious configuration fault that the system detects at startup. The safety program is protected by a password and carries a signature that must be recorded in the acceptance documentation.
chunks.query: PROFIsafe black channel protocol and F-address assignment on a fail-safe CPU

chunks.title: Emergency stop through a fail-safe digital input to SIL 2 and PL d
chunks.text: An emergency stop device is connected to a fail-safe digital input module using two channels so that a single fault does not prevent the stop function. The module performs discrepancy analysis between the channels and applies test pulses to detect short circuits between conductors and cross faults to the supply. Configure the discrepancy time to a value longer than the mechanical difference between the contacts but short enough to detect a genuine fault. This arrangement typically achieves SIL 2 according to the functional safety standard and performance level d, subject to the calculated values for the whole chain. The achieved level depends on the entire function from sensor through logic to actuator, not on the input module alone. Document the calculation and retain it with the machine file.
chunks.query: emergency stop wired to a fail-safe digital input achieving SIL 2 and PL d
chunks.text_ko: 비상 정지 장치는 단일 고장이 정지 기능을 방해하지 않도록 2채널로 페일세이프 디지털 입력 모듈 F-DI에 연결합니다. 모듈은 채널 간 불일치를 분석하고 테스트 펄스를 인가하여 도체 간 단락과 전원으로의 교차 고장을 검출합니다. 불일치 시간은 접점 간 기계적 차이보다는 길고 실제 고장을 검출할 수 있을 만큼은 짧게 설정하십시오. 이 구성은 일반적으로 기능 안전 규격에 따른 SIL 2와 성능 수준 PL d를 달성하지만 전체 체인에 대한 계산 값에 따라 달라집니다. 달성 수준은 입력 모듈 단독이 아니라 센서부터 로직과 액추에이터까지 전체 기능에 의해 결정됩니다. 계산 근거를 문서화하여 기계 파일과 함께 보관하십시오.

chunks.title: Safe Torque Off and Safe Stop 1 on SINAMICS drives
chunks.text: Safe Torque Off removes the pulses to the power semiconductors so that the motor can produce no torque, and it is the base function on which the other safety functions are built. Safe Stop 1 first brakes the motor along a monitored ramp and then activates Safe Torque Off after a configured delay, giving a controlled stop rather than a coast. Note that Safe Torque Off does not apply a mechanical brake, so a suspended vertical load will fall unless a separate brake is fitted and controlled. Select the delay time for Safe Stop 1 by measuring the actual deceleration of the loaded axis rather than by calculation alone. The functions can be triggered over terminals or over PROFIsafe, and the selected method must be consistent with the achieved safety level. Acceptance testing of each configured function is mandatory and must be documented.
chunks.query: Safe Torque Off and Safe Stop 1 functions on the SINAMICS drive
chunks.text_ko: 안전 토크 차단 STO는 전력 반도체로 가는 펄스를 제거하여 모터가 토크를 발생시킬 수 없도록 하는 기능이며 다른 안전 기능의 기반이 됩니다. 안전 정지 1 SS1은 먼저 감시되는 램프를 따라 모터를 제동한 후 설정된 지연 시간이 지나면 STO를 활성화하여 관성 주행이 아닌 제어된 정지를 제공합니다. STO는 기계식 브레이크를 작동시키지 않으므로 수직으로 매달린 부하는 별도의 브레이크를 장착하고 제어하지 않으면 낙하합니다. SS1의 지연 시간은 계산만으로 정하지 말고 부하가 걸린 축의 실제 감속을 측정하여 선정하십시오. 두 기능은 단자 또는 PROFIsafe를 통해 트리거할 수 있으며 선택한 방식은 달성하려는 안전 수준과 일관되어야 합니다. 설정된 각 기능의 인수 시험은 필수이며 문서화해야 합니다.
chunks.query_ko: SINAMICS 드라이브의 STO 안전 토크 차단과 SS1 기능

chunks.title: Muting configuration for material transport through a light curtain
chunks.text: Muting temporarily and automatically suspends the protective function of a light curtain so that material can pass without stopping the machine. The muting sensors must be arranged so that a pallet triggers them in a sequence and within a time window that a person cannot reproduce. A minimum of two independent sensors with a sequence and timing constraint is required, and a single sensor arrangement is never acceptable. The muting condition must end as soon as the material has passed, and a maximum muting duration should be configured so that a stuck sensor cannot leave the guard suspended indefinitely. Muting lamps indicating the suspended state are required so that personnel can see the guard is inactive. Validate the arrangement by attempting to walk through during a muted pass.
chunks.query: letting pallets pass through the light curtain without stopping the machine

chunks.title: Safely Limited Speed monitoring
chunks.text: Safely Limited Speed monitors the actual velocity of an axis against a configured limit and initiates a fault reaction if the limit is exceeded. The function is used to permit access to a hazard zone while the machine continues to move slowly, for example during setup or observation of a process. Velocity is derived from an encoder whose fault detection capability determines the achievable safety level, and a single encoder without additional plausibility checking limits what can be claimed. Configure the fault reaction, typically Safe Stop 1 or Safe Torque Off, according to the risk assessment for the exposed hazard. The tolerance and filter time must be set so that normal speed ripple does not trigger the monitoring while a genuine runaway is caught quickly. Verify the actual trip point by deliberately commanding an overspeed during acceptance testing.
chunks.query: Safely Limited Speed monitoring function and its fault reaction

chunks.title: Interpreting the CPU status and error LEDs
chunks.text: The CPU carries RUN/STOP, ERROR, and MAINT indicators whose combination identifies the broad class of problem before any tool is connected. A steady red ERROR indicator signals a diagnostic event that has been entered in the buffer, while a flashing pattern during startup indicates a firmware or memory card problem. The MAINT indicator requests maintenance without stopping operation, typically for a module reporting a wire break or an approaching limit. A CPU in STOP with no error indication has usually been placed there deliberately by a tool or by a programmed instruction rather than by a fault. Always read the diagnostic buffer rather than relying on the indicators alone, since the buffer carries the timestamp and the originating module. The buffer is retained across a power cycle and is the single most valuable source during fault finding.
chunks.query: what the red ERROR light on the CPU means and where to look next
chunks.text_ko: CPU에는 RUN/STOP, ERROR, MAINT 표시등이 있으며 그 조합만으로도 도구를 연결하기 전에 문제의 대분류를 파악할 수 있습니다. ERROR 표시등이 적색으로 점등되면 버퍼에 진단 이벤트가 기록되었음을 의미하고, 기동 중 점멸 패턴은 펌웨어 또는 메모리 카드 문제를 나타냅니다. MAINT 표시등은 운전을 정지시키지 않고 유지보수를 요청하며 일반적으로 단선이나 한계 접근을 보고하는 모듈에서 발생합니다. 오류 표시 없이 STOP 상태인 CPU는 대개 고장이 아니라 도구나 프로그램 명령에 의해 의도적으로 정지된 것입니다. 버퍼에는 타임스탬프와 발생 모듈이 기록되므로 표시등에만 의존하지 말고 항상 진단 버퍼를 읽으십시오. 버퍼는 전원 재투입 후에도 유지되며 고장 탐구 시 가장 가치 있는 정보원입니다.
chunks.query_ko: CPU의 빨간 ERROR 표시등이 의미하는 것과 다음에 확인할 곳

chunks.title: Passivation and reintegration of fail-safe modules
chunks.text: When a fail-safe module detects a fault it enters a passivated state in which it supplies substitute values of zero to the safety program rather than the process values. Passivation is deliberately sticky, so the module does not return to normal operation automatically even after the underlying fault has cleared. Reintegration requires an explicit acknowledgement, which is normally routed through a variable in the safety program driven by an operator pushbutton. This ensures that a person confirms the situation is safe before the substitute values are replaced by live process data. A module that repeatedly passivates points to an intermittent wiring fault, a cross circuit, or a device whose test pulse tolerance is inadequate. Check the diagnostic buffer for the specific channel and fault type rather than acknowledging repeatedly.
chunks.query: fail-safe module passivation and reintegration acknowledgement

chunks.title: SINAMICS fault F07801 motor overcurrent
chunks.text: Fault F07801 indicates that the drive output current has exceeded the permitted threshold. Frequent causes include an acceleration ramp that is too steep for the connected inertia, a short circuit or earth fault in the motor cable, an incorrectly entered motor data set, and excessive motor cable capacitance from an over-length run. Check first whether the fault occurs only during acceleration, which points to the ramp or the inertia, or also at constant speed, which points to a wiring or motor problem. Verify the entered motor rating plate data, since a mismatch in rated current or pole pair number causes the current controller to be badly tuned. Measure the insulation resistance of the motor and cable if an earth fault is suspected. Do not simply raise the current limit to suppress the fault.
chunks.query: SINAMICS fault F07801 overcurrent on the drive output
chunks.text_ko: 고장 F07801은 SINAMICS 드라이브 출력 전류가 허용 임계값을 초과했음을 나타냅니다. 흔한 원인으로는 연결된 관성에 비해 과도하게 급격한 가속 램프, 모터 케이블의 단락 또는 지락, 잘못 입력된 모터 데이터, 과도한 케이블 길이로 인한 정전 용량 증가가 있습니다. 먼저 고장이 가속 중에만 발생하는지 확인하십시오. 가속 중에만 발생하면 램프나 관성의 문제이고, 정속 운전 중에도 발생하면 배선이나 모터의 문제입니다. 정격 전류나 극쌍수가 일치하지 않으면 전류 제어기가 잘못 튜닝되므로 입력한 모터 명판 데이터를 검증하십시오. 지락이 의심되면 모터와 케이블의 절연 저항을 측정하십시오. 고장을 억제하기 위해 단순히 전류 제한값을 높이지 마십시오.
chunks.query_ko: SINAMICS 드라이브 출력 과전류 고장 F07801

chunks.title: Diagnosing a PROFINET station failure
chunks.text: A station failure is reported when the controller stops receiving cyclic frames from a configured device within the watchdog period. Read the diagnostic buffer to identify which station dropped and whether the failure is isolated or affects a group of devices sharing a physical path. A group failure normally indicates a cable, connector, or switch problem at the point where the affected branch joins, rather than a fault in the individual devices. Check the port statistics for discarded frames and CRC errors, which reveal a marginal physical link that has not yet failed outright. A device that fails only under vibration or temperature change usually has a poorly terminated connector. Replacing a device without first checking the physical layer statistics frequently just moves the fault.
chunks.query: PROFINET station failure diagnostics and checking port error counters
chunks.text_ko: 설정된 장치로부터 감시 시간 내에 주기적 프레임 수신이 중단되면 스테이션 고장이 보고됩니다. 진단 버퍼를 읽어 어느 스테이션이 탈락했는지, 그리고 고장이 단독인지 물리 경로를 공유하는 장치 그룹에 영향을 미치는지 확인하십시오. 그룹 고장은 일반적으로 개별 장치의 결함이 아니라 해당 분기가 합류하는 지점의 케이블, 커넥터, 스위치 문제를 나타냅니다. 아직 완전히 끊어지지는 않았지만 한계 상태인 물리 링크를 드러내는 폐기 프레임과 CRC 오류 카운터를 확인하십시오. 진동이나 온도 변화가 있을 때만 고장 나는 장치는 대개 커넥터 압착 불량이 원인입니다. 물리 계층 통계를 먼저 확인하지 않고 장치를 교체하면 고장 위치만 옮겨지는 경우가 많습니다.
chunks.query_ko: PROFINET 스테이션 고장 진단과 포트 오류 카운터 확인

chunks.title: Controller halts when the permitted execution time is exceeded
chunks.text: The processor supervises how long the cyclic program takes to complete and halts if the configured maximum is exceeded, because an overrun means the process is no longer being served at the expected rate. Frequent triggers are an unbounded loop, a communication instruction waiting on an unresponsive partner, or a large data operation placed in the main cyclic block. Interrupt routines that themselves take too long can also push the total beyond the limit even though the main block is unchanged. Inspect the recorded execution time statistics to distinguish a gradual growth, which suggests accumulating data volume, from a sudden jump, which suggests a code change. Raising the permitted time is occasionally correct but usually masks a design problem that will worsen. Move long-running operations into a lower priority task rather than extending the limit.
chunks.query: the processor keeps dropping out of run mode because something in the program takes too long
chunks.text_ko: 프로세서는 주기적 프로그램의 완료 시간을 감시하며 설정된 최대값을 초과하면 정지합니다. 초과는 공정이 더 이상 예상 속도로 처리되지 않음을 의미하기 때문입니다. 빈번한 원인은 종료 조건이 없는 반복문, 응답하지 않는 상대와의 통신 명령 대기, 주 주기 블록에 배치된 대용량 데이터 연산입니다. 인터럽트 루틴 자체가 너무 오래 걸리면 주 블록이 변경되지 않았더라도 전체 시간이 한계를 넘을 수 있습니다. 기록된 실행 시간 통계를 확인하여 데이터 누적을 시사하는 점진적 증가인지 코드 변경을 시사하는 급격한 상승인지 구분하십시오. 허용 시간을 늘리는 것이 옳은 경우도 가끔 있지만 대개는 악화될 설계 문제를 가리는 것입니다. 한계를 늘리는 대신 오래 걸리는 연산을 낮은 우선순위 태스크로 옮기십시오.
chunks.query_ko: 프로그램에서 뭔가가 너무 오래 걸려서 프로세서가 자꾸 운전 상태에서 떨어집니다

chunks.title: Replacing the removable storage medium in the processor
chunks.text: The program and configuration reside on a removable card rather than in internal memory, which means a replacement processor can be brought into service simply by transferring the card. The card must be present for the processor to leave the stopped state, and removing it during operation halts the unit immediately. Format the card only with the engineering tool or through the processor itself, because formatting in a standard card reader destroys the required internal structure. Keep a written record of which card belongs to which machine, since the cards are physically identical and a mix-up during a shutdown is easy. Store a spare programmed card with the machine documentation for rapid recovery. The card also holds the archived diagnostic data, which is lost if the card is reformatted.
chunks.query: we are swapping in a spare processor unit and need the machine running again without a laptop

chunks.title: Retentive data and behaviour across power failure
chunks.text: Retentive data survives a power failure and a warm restart, and is held in a maintenance-free buffered area rather than requiring a battery on current hardware. Declare only the variables that genuinely need to survive, since an oversized retentive area lengthens startup and complicates commissioning. Understand the difference between a warm restart, which retains the declared data, and a cold restart, which initialises everything to the configured start values. Counters and accumulated production totals are the most common candidates for retention, while intermediate calculation results generally should not be retained. Test the behaviour deliberately by removing power mid-cycle during commissioning and confirming the machine resumes in a defined state. An undefined resume state after power failure is a frequent source of scrap on the first production morning.
chunks.query: which values survive a power cut and how does the machine come back afterwards

chunks.title: Firmware update of the CPU and distributed modules
chunks.text: Firmware is updated from the engineering tool over the network or by placing an update file on the memory card and cycling power. Distributed I/O modules and drives each carry their own firmware and may need updating separately to remain compatible with the CPU version. Read the compatibility matrix before starting, since a CPU updated in isolation may refuse to communicate with a device left on an older version. Back up the full project and archive the existing firmware versions before proceeding. Never interrupt power during an update, as a partially written firmware image can leave a module requiring factory recovery. Schedule updates during a planned shutdown with sufficient time to validate the machine afterwards.
chunks.query: updating firmware on the CPU and the distributed IO modules
chunks.text_ko: 펌웨어는 엔지니어링 도구에서 네트워크를 통해 갱신하거나 메모리 카드에 갱신 파일을 넣고 전원을 재투입하여 갱신합니다. 분산 입출력 모듈과 드라이브는 각각 자체 펌웨어를 가지고 있으며 CPU 버전과의 호환성을 유지하려면 별도로 갱신해야 할 수 있습니다. CPU만 단독으로 갱신하면 구버전에 남은 장치와 통신을 거부할 수 있으므로 시작 전에 호환성 표를 확인하십시오. 진행 전에 전체 프로젝트를 백업하고 기존 펌웨어 버전을 보관하십시오. 펌웨어 이미지가 부분적으로만 기록되면 모듈이 공장 복구를 요구하는 상태가 될 수 있으므로 갱신 중에는 절대 전원을 차단하지 마십시오. 갱신은 이후 기계를 검증할 충분한 시간이 확보된 계획 정지 기간에 수행하십시오.
chunks.query_ko: CPU와 분산 IO 모듈의 펌웨어를 갱신하는 방법

chunks.title: Cooling fan and filter mat servicing in the drive cabinet
chunks.text: Cooling fans in drive units are wear parts with a defined service life, typically expressed in operating hours at a stated ambient temperature and reducing sharply as temperature rises. Replace fans preventively at the stated interval rather than waiting for failure, because a drive that trips on overtemperature during production costs far more than the part. Filter mats must be inspected and cleaned or replaced on a schedule matched to the environment, which may be weekly where dust or fibre is present. A blocked filter reduces airflow gradually, so the drive runs progressively hotter for months before finally tripping. Record the ambient temperature trend if available, as a rising baseline is the clearest early indicator. Keep spare fans and mats on site for the frame sizes installed.
chunks.query: the drive trips out on heat late in the shift and it has been getting worse over several months

chunks.title: Reforming the DC link capacitors of stored equipment
chunks.text: The electrolytic capacitors in the DC link of a drive degrade when the unit is left unpowered for an extended period, because the oxide layer that forms the dielectric slowly dissolves. A unit stored for more than one year should be reformed by applying a controlled voltage through a current-limiting arrangement before being placed into service. Applying full mains voltage directly to a long-stored drive can cause a violent capacitor failure. The reforming procedure and the required duration depend on how long the unit has been stored, with longer storage requiring a longer and more gradual process. This applies equally to spare units held in a store room, which is frequently overlooked until the spare is urgently needed and fails on first energisation. Record the storage date on every spare and rotate the stock through a periodic energisation.
chunks.query: a spare unit that sat in the store room for three years blew up as soon as we energised it
chunks.text_ko: 드라이브 직류 링크의 전해 커패시터는 유전체를 형성하는 산화막이 서서히 용해되기 때문에 장기간 전원을 인가하지 않고 보관하면 열화됩니다. 1년 이상 보관한 장치는 사용 전에 전류 제한 장치를 통해 제어된 전압을 인가하여 재성형해야 합니다. 장기간 보관한 드라이브에 상용 전압을 직접 인가하면 커패시터가 격렬하게 파손될 수 있습니다. 재성형 절차와 소요 시간은 보관 기간에 따라 달라지며 보관 기간이 길수록 더 길고 점진적인 과정이 필요합니다. 이는 창고에 보관 중인 예비품에도 동일하게 적용되지만, 예비품이 급히 필요해져 처음 통전할 때 고장 나기 전까지 간과되는 경우가 많습니다. 모든 예비품에 보관 일자를 기록하고 주기적으로 통전하여 재고를 순환시키십시오.
chunks.query_ko: 창고에 3년 동안 두었던 예비 장치를 전원에 연결하자마자 터져버렸습니다

chunks.title: Choosing between SCL and ladder in TIA Portal
chunks.text: Structured Control Language is a textual high level language suited to algorithms, loops, string handling, and mathematical computation. Ladder logic remains the natural choice for interlocking, sequencing, and any logic that maintenance staff will need to read on a panel during a breakdown. A mixed approach is normal and appropriate: implement the machine interlocks in ladder so they can be traced visually, and implement data processing in a structured language block called from that ladder. Avoid writing complex arithmetic in ladder using chained move and compare instructions, which is both error prone and unreadable. Consider who will maintain the machine at three in the morning when selecting the language for a given block. Comment blocks in both languages, since neither is self-documenting at scale.
chunks.query: when to use SCL versus ladder logic in TIA Portal

chunks.title: Organisation blocks and the cyclic program structure
chunks.text: The main cyclic program executes in the primary organisation block, which the operating system calls repeatedly for as long as the processor is running. Additional organisation blocks handle startup, time-based interrupts, hardware interrupts, and error conditions, each with its own priority. A cyclic interrupt block executes at a fixed interval independent of the main cycle and is the correct place for closed loop control code that requires a constant sample time. Error handling blocks allow a diagnostic event that would otherwise halt the processor to be caught and managed, but their presence should not be used to hide genuine faults. Keep high priority blocks short, because they interrupt the main cycle and contribute directly to the total execution time. Document the priority scheme, as an unexpected interaction between priorities is difficult to diagnose later.
chunks.query: how the main program block and interrupt blocks fit together in the scan

chunks.title: Optimised and standard data block access
chunks.text: Data blocks can be declared with optimised access, in which the system arranges the variables in memory for efficient access, or with standard access, in which the layout is fixed and byte addressable. Optimised blocks are faster and safer because variables are reached symbolically and cannot be corrupted by an incorrect absolute address. Standard access remains necessary when an external system or an older function requires a byte offset into the block, such as some communication instructions and legacy library code. Mixing the two unnecessarily creates confusion, and converting a block between the modes changes how every reference to it behaves. Prefer optimised access for new development and confine standard access to the specific interfaces that demand it. Note that the initial values and retention behaviour differ subtly between the two modes.
chunks.query: optimised versus standard data block access

chunks.title: Technology objects for positioning axes
chunks.text: A positioning axis is configured as a technology object that encapsulates the mechanical parameters, the encoder assignment, the dynamic limits, and the homing behaviour. Motion is then commanded through standard instruction blocks that reference the object rather than by writing directly to the drive telegram. Configure the mechanical ratio carefully so that the programmed units correspond to real world movement, since an error here scales every subsequent position. Dynamic limits for velocity, acceleration, and jerk should reflect the mechanics rather than the maximum the drive can deliver. The object provides status and error information that should be evaluated in the program rather than assumed successful. Use the commissioning panel to move the axis manually and validate direction, scaling, and limits before writing any program logic.
chunks.query: configuring a positioning axis technology object and its dynamic limits
chunks.text_ko: 위치 결정 축은 기계 파라미터, 엔코더 할당, 동특성 한계, 원점 복귀 동작을 캡슐화하는 테크놀로지 오브젝트로 구성됩니다. 이후 동작은 드라이브 텔레그램에 직접 기록하는 대신 해당 오브젝트를 참조하는 표준 명령 블록을 통해 지령합니다. 여기서 오차가 발생하면 이후 모든 위치에 배율로 작용하므로 프로그래밍 단위가 실제 이동량과 일치하도록 기계 비율을 신중하게 설정하십시오. 속도, 가속도, 저크의 동특성 한계는 드라이브가 낼 수 있는 최대치가 아니라 기계 성능을 반영해야 합니다. 오브젝트는 상태와 오류 정보를 제공하므로 성공을 가정하지 말고 프로그램에서 평가해야 합니다. 프로그램 로직을 작성하기 전에 시운전 패널로 축을 수동 이동시켜 방향, 배율, 한계를 검증하십시오.
chunks.query_ko: 위치 결정 축 테크놀로지 오브젝트 설정과 동특성 한계

chunks.title: Connecting operator panel displays to controller variables
chunks.text: Values shown on an operator display are bound to controller variables through a tag connection defined in the visualisation project. Where the display and the controller are engineered in the same project, tags can reference controller symbols directly and remain consistent when a symbol is renamed. An externally engineered display uses an area pointer and absolute addressing, which breaks silently when the controller data layout changes. Choose acquisition cycles deliberately, because a screen full of fast-updating values loads both the network and the panel processor without benefit to the operator. Values that change slowly should be polled slowly. A panel that becomes sluggish after a screen is added is nearly always suffering from excessive acquisition rates rather than insufficient hardware.
chunks.query: the touchscreen got very sluggish after we added a new page full of readings

chunks.title: PROFINET device names and address assignment
chunks.text: PROFINET identifies devices by a device name rather than by an IP address, and the name must be assigned to the physical device before it can be addressed by the controller. Assignment is performed online from the engineering tool, and the name written into the device must exactly match the name in the hardware configuration. A replaced device arrives with an empty name and will not communicate until the name is assigned, which is why device replacement without a laptop requires the neighbourhood-based automatic assignment feature to be configured in advance. IP addresses are then assigned by the controller at startup based on the configured name. A duplicate device name on the network prevents both devices from establishing a connection. Record the naming scheme in the cell documentation.
chunks.query: PROFINET device name assignment and automatic device replacement

chunks.title: Topology configuration and media redundancy
chunks.text: Configuring the physical topology in the engineering tool records which port of each device connects to which port of its neighbour. This enables precise diagnostics, since the system can report exactly which link has failed rather than merely that a station is absent, and it is a prerequisite for neighbourhood-based device replacement. A media redundancy ring allows the network to survive a single cable break by reconfiguring around the fault, with one device acting as the ring manager. Reconfiguration takes a finite time during which cyclic communication is interrupted, so the configured watchdog must tolerate that interruption. Do not close a ring physically without configuring the redundancy protocol, as the resulting loop will saturate the network with circulating frames. Verify redundancy by breaking each link in turn during commissioning.
chunks.query: setting up a redundant ring so a single cable break does not stop the line

chunks.title: Update time and reduction ratio for cyclic data exchange
chunks.text: Each device is assigned an interval at which its cyclic data is exchanged with the controller, derived from the send clock and a reduction ratio. Setting every device to the fastest available interval consumes bandwidth and processor resources without improving anything for devices whose signals change slowly. Match the interval to the actual dynamics of the connected process: a temperature sensor does not need the same rate as a high speed position input. The accepted number of consecutive missed frames before a station is declared failed multiplies the interval to give the effective watchdog, which must exceed any expected reconfiguration time. An aggressive combination of a short interval and a low missed-frame count produces intermittent station failures on an otherwise healthy network. Review these settings when adding devices to an established network.
chunks.query: we added more devices and now stations drop out at random even though the cabling tests fine

chunks.title: OPC UA server on the S7-1500 controller
chunks.text: The controller includes an OPC UA server that exposes selected variables to higher level systems without requiring a dedicated gateway. The server requires a licence and must be explicitly enabled in the hardware configuration, after which individual variables and blocks are marked as accessible. Restrict the exposed set deliberately rather than publishing the entire symbol table, both for performance and to avoid coupling external systems to internal implementation details. Configure certificate-based security and disable anonymous access before connecting the controller to any network beyond the cell. Server methods can be defined to allow a client to invoke a controlled action rather than writing directly to variables, which is generally the safer integration pattern. Monitor the number of concurrent sessions against the licensed limit.
chunks.query: enabling the OPC UA server on the S7-1500 and exposing variables

chunks.title: Clock synchronised operation for coordinated motion
chunks.text: Isochronous operation synchronises the acquisition of input data, the execution of the user program, and the output of results to a common network clock. This removes the variable delay that otherwise exists between a signal changing and the program acting on it, which is essential when several axes must be coordinated precisely or when position must be captured at an exact instant. All participating devices and the network path must support the mode, and the topology must be configured. The program portion that processes the synchronised data runs in a dedicated organisation block whose execution must reliably complete within the allotted portion of the cycle. Configuring the mode without respecting the timing budget produces cycle overruns rather than improved performance. Use it only where the application genuinely requires deterministic coordination.
chunks.query: several axes need to move in exact step with each other and with a sensor reading

chunks.title: Drive commissioning and motor data identification
chunks.text: Commissioning a drive begins with entering the motor rating plate data, after which an automatic identification routine measures the actual electrical characteristics of the connected motor and cable. The routine energises the motor and may rotate it, so the mechanics must be clear and the axis must be free to turn or explicitly configured for a stationary measurement. Identification substantially improves control quality because the calculated values from the rating plate alone do not account for cable resistance or manufacturing tolerance. Repeat the identification if the motor or the motor cable is changed, as the measured values include the cable. A drive that runs roughly at low speed or draws unexpected current very often has never had the identification performed. Record the resulting parameter set as part of the commissioning archive.
chunks.query: motor data identification routine when commissioning a new drive
chunks.text_ko: 드라이브 시운전은 모터 명판 데이터 입력으로 시작하며, 이후 자동 식별 루틴이 연결된 모터와 케이블의 실제 전기적 특성을 측정합니다. 이 루틴은 모터에 전류를 인가하며 회전시킬 수 있으므로 기계부가 비어 있어야 하고 축이 자유롭게 회전할 수 있거나 정지 상태 측정으로 명시적으로 설정되어 있어야 합니다. 명판만으로 계산한 값은 케이블 저항이나 제조 공차를 반영하지 못하므로 식별을 수행하면 제어 품질이 크게 향상됩니다. 측정값에는 케이블이 포함되므로 모터나 모터 케이블을 교체한 경우 식별을 다시 수행하십시오. 저속에서 거칠게 회전하거나 예상 밖의 전류를 소비하는 드라이브는 식별을 한 번도 수행하지 않은 경우가 매우 많습니다. 결과 파라미터 세트를 시운전 기록의 일부로 보관하십시오.
chunks.query_ko: 새 드라이브를 시운전할 때 수행하는 모터 데이터 식별 루틴

chunks.title: Determining the rotor position reference for a synchronous motor
chunks.text: A permanent magnet synchronous motor requires the controller to know the angular relationship between the encoder zero and the magnetic field of the rotor. If this offset is wrong the current is injected at the wrong electrical angle, producing weak or reversed torque, excessive current for the torque delivered, and a motor that runs away or refuses to start. The offset is determined by an identification routine that injects test signals and observes the response, and it must be repeated whenever the encoder is disturbed relative to the shaft. Symptoms of an incorrect offset include the axis jumping at enable, drawing high current while barely moving, or accelerating uncontrollably in one direction. This value is specific to the motor and encoder pairing and cannot be copied from another axis. Record the identified value so a repeat can be verified against it.

chunks.title: Establishing a known absolute position on an incremental system
chunks.text: An axis fitted with an incremental measuring system knows only relative movement at power-up and must establish a defined starting point before absolute positions become meaningful. The usual method drives the axis toward a proximity switch at a search velocity, then reverses at a slower velocity to locate a precise encoder marker, giving a repeatable result independent of the switch tolerance. Choose the approach direction so that the axis always arrives from the same side, eliminating the effect of mechanical lost motion. The switch must be positioned so that the axis cannot overrun the mechanical limit if the search fails to find it. An absolute measuring system does not require this procedure, but its offset must still be established once during commissioning. Verify by returning to the reference from several starting positions and confirming the recorded value repeats.

chunks.title: Tuning the velocity controller for a loaded axis
chunks.text: The velocity controller gain determines how aggressively the drive corrects a speed deviation, and it must be matched to the total inertia and the stiffness of the mechanical coupling. Excessive gain causes an audible whine and a visible oscillation, while insufficient gain produces sluggish response and large following error under load. An automatic tuning function excites the axis and derives suitable values from the measured response, which is a good starting point but rarely the final answer for a machine with compliance or backlash. A belt driven or long shaft coupled axis has a resonance that limits the usable gain, and a filter tuned to that frequency allows a higher gain to be used safely. Always tune with the real load fitted, since values found on an unloaded motor will not transfer. Verify across the full travel, as inertia may vary with position on some mechanisms.

chunks.title: Determining the reflected inertia of the driven load
chunks.text: The ratio between the inertia of the driven load reflected to the motor shaft and the inertia of the motor itself is the single most important number for predicting achievable control performance. A high ratio makes the axis difficult to control and limits the usable gain, particularly where the coupling is compliant. The value can be measured by an identification routine that accelerates the axis at a known torque and observes the resulting rate of change of speed. Entering a value that is too low leads the controller to expect a faster response than the mechanism can deliver, producing overshoot and instability. Where the load changes during operation, such as a rotating table carrying different fixtures, tune for the worst case or switch parameter sets. Recheck the value after any mechanical modification to the driven equipment.
